translations.text: Prologue
Because many have undertaken to set in order the account of the things that have been fulfilled among us,
just as those who from the beginning saw for themselves and were ministers of the word handed them down to us,
it seemed good to me also, having followed all things carefully from the beginning, to write them to you in order, most excellent Theophilus,
so that you may understand the truth of the words in which you have been instructed.
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and God himself was the Word.
It was in the beginning with God. All things were made through it, and without it nothing was made that was made.
That which was in him was life, and the life was the light of men.
And the light shone in the darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it.
In the days of Herod, the king of the Jews, there was a certain priest named Zacharias, of the course of Abijah, and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.
They were both righteous before God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and ordinances of God. And they had no son, because Elizabeth was barren, and both were advanced in their days.

Then it happened, while he was serving in the priesthood in the order of his course before God, that according to the custom of the priesthood the lot fell to him to burn incense, entering into God's temple. And the whole multitude of the people was praying outside at the time of the incense offering.
An angel of God appeared to him, standing at the right side of the altar of incense. Then Zacharias was troubled when he saw this, and fear fell upon him.
Then the angel said to him: "Do not be afraid, Zacharias, for your prayer has been heard, and your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you shall call his name John.

And he will be joy and gladness to you, and many will rejoice at his birth. For he will be great before the Lord, and he will drink neither wine nor strong drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother's womb. And he will turn many of the children of Israel to the Lord their God.

And he will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children, and the unbelieving to the wisdom of the righteous, to make ready for the Lord a perfect people."
And Zacharias said to the angel: "How shall I know this? I am old, and my wife is advanced in her days."

Then the angel answered and said to him: "I am Gabriel, who stands before God, and I have been sent to you to tell you these things. And now you will be silent and unable to speak until the day on which these things come to pass, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled in their time."

And the people were waiting for Zacharias, and they wondered that he was delaying in the temple. When he came out he could not speak to them, and they understood that he had seen a vision in the temple. He kept making signs to them and remained mute.

And when the days of his service were completed, he went to his house. After those days Elizabeth his wife conceived, and she hid herself for five months, saying: "For thus the Lord has done to me in the days in which he looked on me, to take away my reproach among men."
In the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent by God to a city of Galilee called Nazareth, to a virgin betrothed to a man named Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary.
And the angel came in to her and said: "Hail, you who are full of grace! The Lord is with you; blessed are you among women."
When she saw this, she was troubled at his word and wondered what this greeting could be.
The angel said to her: "Do not be afraid, Mary; you have found favour with God. Behold, you will conceive in your womb and bear a son, and you will call his name Jesus."

"He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High, and the Lord will give him the throne of his father David, and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and of his kingdom there will be no end."
Then Mary said to the angel: "How can this be, since I do not know a man?"

Then the angel answered and said to her: "The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; therefore the holy one who will be born will be called the Son of God."
"Behold, Elizabeth your kinswoman has also conceived a son in her old age, and this is the sixth month for her who is called barren; for no word is impossible with God."
Then Mary said: "Behold the handmaid of God; let it be to me according to your word." And then the angel departed from her.
In those days Mary arose and went with haste into the hill country, to a city of Judah, and entered the house of Zechariah and greeted Elizabeth.
And it happened that when Elizabeth heard Mary's greeting, the child leapt in her womb.

Then Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit, and she cried out with a loud voice and said: "Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb! And why is this granted to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?"

"For behold, as soon as the voice of your greeting came to my ears, the child in my womb leapt for joy. And blessed is she who believed, for the things that were spoken to her by the Lord will be fulfilled."
Then Mary said: "My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit has rejoiced in God my Saviour, for he has looked upon the lowliness of his handmaid."

"For behold, from now on all generations will call me blessed, for he who is mighty has done great things for me, and holy is his name, and his mercy is from generation to generation on those who fear him."

"He has shown strength with his arm; he has scattered the proud in the mind of their heart; he has put down the mighty from their seat and exalted the humble; he has filled the hungry with good things, and the rich he has sent away empty."
"He has taken up Israel his servant, in remembrance of his mercy, as he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed forever."
Mary stayed with her about three months, and returned to her own house.
Now the time was fulfilled for Elizabeth to give birth, and she bore a son.
And her neighbours and her kinsfolk heard that the Lord had shown great mercy to her, and they rejoiced with her.

Then it came to pass on the eighth day that they came to circumcise the child, and they named him by his father's name, Zacharias. Then his mother answered and said: "Not at all, but his name shall be John." And they said to her: "There is no one in your kindred who is called by this name."

Then they made signs to his father, what he would have him called. Then he asked for a writing tablet and wrote, saying thus: "John is his name." Then they all marveled at that. Then his mouth and his tongue were opened at once, and he spoke, blessing God.

Then fear came upon all their neighbors, and all these words were made known throughout all the hill country of Judea; and all who heard it laid it up in their hearts, saying thus: "What do you think this child will be?" And the hand of God was with him.

And Zacharias his father was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying thus: "Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, because he has visited and brought redemption to his people, and has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of David his servant,

as he spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets, who have been since the beginning of the world: salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all who hated us; to show mercy to our fathers and to remember his holy covenant, the oath which he swore to Abraham our father, to grant us
that, delivered without fear from the hands of our enemies, we might serve him in holiness and in righteousness before him all our days.

And you, child, shall be called the prophet of the Most High; for you shall go before the face of the Lord to prepare his way, to give knowledge of salvation to his people in the forgiveness of their sins,

through the inmost mercy of our God, by which the dayspring from on high has visited us, to give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace."
The child grew and was strengthened in spirit, and was in the wilderness until the day of his manifestation to Israel.

The book of the generation of the Savior Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham: Abraham begot Isaac. Isaac begot Jacob. Jacob begot Judah and his brothers. Judah begot Perez and Zerah by Tamar. Perez begot Hezron. Hezron begot Ram. Ram begot Amminadab. Amminadab begot Nahshon. Nahshon begot Salmon. Salmon begot Boaz by Rahab. Boaz begot Obed by Ruth. Obed begot Jesse. Jesse begot David the king.

David the king begot Solomon. Solomon begot Rehoboam. Rehoboam begot Abijah. Abijah begot Asa. Asa begot Jehoshaphat. Jehoshaphat begot Joram. Joram begot Uzziah. Uzziah begot Jotham. Jotham begot Ahaz. Ahaz begot Hezekiah. Hezekiah begot Manasseh. Manasseh begot Amon. Amon begot Josiah.

Josiah begot Jechoniah and his brothers at the time of the deportation to Babylon. And after the deportation to Babylon, Jechoniah begot Shealtiel. Shealtiel begot Zerubbabel. Zerubbabel begot Abiud. Abiud begot Eliakim. Eliakim begot Azor. Azor begot Zadok. Zadok begot Eliakim. Eliakim begot Eliud. Eliud begot Eleazar. Eleazar begot Matthan. Matthan begot Jacob.

Jacob begot Joseph, the husband of Mary, of whom was born the Savior, who is called Christ. Abraham was the son of Terah, who was the son of Nahor, who was the son of Serug, who was the son of Reu, who was the son of Peleg, who was the son of Eber, who was the son of Shelah, who was the son of Cainan, who was the son of Arphaxad, who was the son of Shem, who was the son of Noah, who was the son of Lamech, who was the son of Methuselah, who was the son of Enoch, who was the son of Jared, who was the son of Mahalalel, who was the son of Cainan,
who was the son of Enos, who was the son of Seth, who was the son of Adam, who was the son of God.
All the generations from Abraham to David were fourteen generations, and from David to the departure to Babylon fourteen generations, and from the departure to Babylon to Christ fourteen generations.

The lineage of Christ was thus: When the Savior's mother Mary was betrothed to Joseph, before they came together, she was found to be with child by the Holy Spirit. Then Joseph her husband, since he was a righteous man and did not want to expose her, wanted to put her away secretly.

As he was thinking this, suddenly an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said: Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary your betrothed, for what is born in her is of the Holy Spirit. She will bear a son, and you shall call his name Savior, because he will save his people from their sins.

All this was done so that what had been spoken by the Lord through the prophet would be fulfilled, who said: Behold, a virgin will conceive in her womb and bear a son, and they will call his name Emmanuel, which is interpreted: God with us.
Then Joseph, rising from sleep, did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him and took his betrothed, and he did not know her until she bore her firstborn son, and he called his name Savior.

It came to pass in those days that a command went out from the all-ruling emperor that all this world should be enrolled. This enrollment was first made in Syria by the governor Quirinius, and all went to register their obligation of service, each in his own city.

Then Joseph went from Galilee, from the city called Nazareth, into the land of the Jews, to the city of David, which was called Bethlehem, because he was of the house and family of David, so that he might register together with Mary, his betrothed wife, who was with child.

While they were there, the days were fulfilled for her to give birth, and she bore her firstborn son and wrapped him in cloths and laid him in a manger, because there was no other place for them in the inn.

There were shepherds in that region, keeping watch and holding the night watch over their flock. An angel of God came there and stood near them, and the brightness of God shone around them; and they were afraid with great fear.

And the angel said to them: Do not be afraid; I bring you news of great joy, which is for all the people, because today the Savior is born to you, who is Christ the Lord, in the city of David. Let this be a sign to you: you will find a child wrapped in cloths and laid in a manger.
Then suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host, praising God and saying: "Glory be to God in the highest, and on earth be peace to men of good will."

Then it happened that the angels went away from them into heaven. Then the shepherds said among themselves: "Let us go to Bethlehem and see this word that has come to pass there, which the Lord has shown us." And they came in haste and found Mary and Joseph, and the child laid in a manger.
Then, when they saw it, they understood the word that had been spoken to them about the child. And all who heard it wondered at it, and at the things the shepherds had told them.
But Mary kept all these words, pondering them in her heart.
Then the shepherds returned home, glorifying and praising God for all the things they had heard and seen, just as it had been told to them.
After eight days had passed and the child was to be circumcised, he was given the name Jesus (the Saviour). This name had been given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.

And after the days of her purification according to the law of Moses were completed, they brought him to Jerusalem to present him to God, as it is written in the law of God: "For every male child that first opens the womb shall be called holy to God."
And they came to give an offering according to what is said in the law of the Lord: a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.

Now behold, there was a man in Jerusalem whose name was Simeon. This man was righteous and God-fearing, waiting for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was in him. He had received an answer from the Holy Spirit that he would not die before he had seen Christ the Lord.
Then he came in the Spirit into the house of God. And when his parents brought in the child Jesus to do for him according to the custom of the law, he took him in his arms and praised God and said:

"Now, Lord, you let your servant go in peace, according to your word, because my eyes have seen your salvation, which you have prepared before the face of all peoples: a light for revelation to the nations and for the glory of your people Israel."
His father and mother wondered at the things that were said about him. And Simeon blessed them and said to Mary his mother:

"Behold, this child is set for the fall and for the rising again of many in Israel, and for a sign that will be spoken against. And a sword will pierce through your own soul, so that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed."

There was also Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher. She was far advanced in years and had lived with her husband seven years after her virginity, and she was a widow until the age of eighty-four. She never left the temple, but served with fasting and prayer day and night.
Coming up at that same hour, she praised the Lord and spoke of him to all who were waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem.
And when they had done everything according to the law of the Lord, they returned to Galilee, to their town of Nazareth.

When the Saviour was born in Bethlehem, a city of the Jews, in the days of King Herod, behold, magi came from the east to Jerusalem, saying: "Where is he who is born king of the Jews? We have seen his star in the east and have come to worship him."
When King Herod heard this, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him. He gathered the chief men among the priests and the scribes of the people and asked them where Christ was to be born.

Then they said to him: "In Bethlehem, a city of the Jews. For so it is written through the prophet: 'You, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are by no means the least among the princes of Judah, for out of you shall come a leader who shall rule my people Israel.'"

Then Herod secretly called the magi and diligently learned from them the time of the star that had appeared to them. He sent them to Bethlehem, saying: "Go and inquire diligently about the child; when you find him, report it to me, so that I may come there and worship him."
When they had heard the king, they went on their way; and behold, the star that they had seen in the east went before them, until it came and stood over the place where the child was.
When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy. Going into the house, they found the child with Mary his mother, and falling down they worshipped him.
And opening their treasure chests, they brought him gifts: gold and frankincense and myrrh.
And having received an answer in a dream that they should not return to Herod, they returned to their own country by another way.
When they had gone away from there, at once an angel of God appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying:
"Arise, take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and stay there until I tell you; for it is about to happen that Herod will seek the child to destroy him."
He then arose and took the child and his mother by night and went into Egypt, and was there until the death of Herod,
so that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying: "Out of Egypt I have called my son."

When Herod saw that he had been deceived by the magi, he was exceedingly angry, and he sent and killed all the boys who were in Bethlehem and in all its borders, from two years old and under, according to the time that he had inquired of the magi.
Then was fulfilled what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet, saying:
"A voice was heard on high, of great weeping and wailing: Rachel weeping for her sons, and she would not be comforted, because they were no more."

When Herod had died, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt, saying: "Arise, take the child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel; for those who sought the child's life are dead."
He then arose, took the child and his mother, and came into the land of Israel.
When he heard that Archelaus reigned in Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there.
And being warned in a dream, he went into the region of Galilee, and when he came there, he dwelt in the city that is called Nazareth;
So that what had been spoken through the prophets might be fulfilled: for he will be called a Nazarene.
The child truly grew and became strong, full of wisdom, and the grace of God was in him. And his parents went every year to Jerusalem on the feast day of Passover.

And when he had become twelve years old, as they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast day, and when the days were completed and they returned home, the boy Jesus remained in Jerusalem, and his parents did not know it.

Thinking that he was in the company of travellers, they went a day's journey and looked for him among their relatives and acquaintances; and not finding him, they went back to Jerusalem looking for him.
Then it happened that after three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.
Then all who heard him were astonished at his wisdom and his answers, and those who saw him marvelled.
Then his mother said to him: "Son, why have you done this to us? Your father and I have been looking for you in sorrow."
And he said to them: "Why is it that you were looking for me? Did you not know that I must be in the things that are my Father's?"
And they did not understand the word that he spoke to them. And going down with them, he came to Nazareth and was subject to them.
And his mother kept all these words in her heart. And Jesus increased in wisdom and in age and in grace with God and with people.

In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, when Pontius Pilate was governing Judea, Herod holding lordship in Galilee, and his brother Philip ruler in the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias ruler in the city that was called Abilene, under the high priests Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came upon John, the son of Zechariah, in the wilderness.
And he came into all the region of the Jordan, preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins, saying thus: "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is drawing near."

This is the one who was proclaimed through the prophet Isaiah, saying thus: "The voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight. Every valley shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be brought low, and the crooked shall become straight and the rough into smooth ways, and all flesh shall see the salvation of God."

He came as a witness, to bear witness of the light, so that all might believe through him. He was not the light, but came to bear witness of the light. That was the true light, which enlightens every person coming into this world.
He was in the world, and the world was made through him, and the world did not know him. He came to his own, and his own did not receive him.

But as many as received him, to them he gave power to become sons of God, to those who believed in his name: who were born not of blood, nor of the desire of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.
And the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us, and we saw his glory, such as is the glory of the only-begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth.
John bears witness of him and cries out, saying thus: This is he of whom I said to you: he who is coming after me has been made before me, because he was before me.
And of his fullness we all receive, even grace for grace, because the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came about through the Saviour Christ.
No one has ever seen God at any time; the only-begotten Son, who is in the Father, he has made it known.
This same John had clothing of camels' hair and a leather girdle about his loins; his food was locusts and wild honey.
Then Jerusalem and all Judea and all the region around the Jordan went out to him, and they were baptized by him in the Jordan, confessing their sins.
When he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism, he said to them: Brood of vipers, who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?

Truly bring forth fruit worthy of your repentance, and do not presume to say among yourselves: We have Abraham as our father. I say to you that God is able to raise up children of Abraham from these stones.
Already the axe is laid to the root of the trees; every tree that does not bear good fruit will be cut down and cast into the fire.
Then the crowds asked him and said: What shall we do? He answered and said to them: Whoever has two tunics, let him give to the one who has none; whoever has food, let him do likewise.
Then the tax collectors came to be baptized, and they said to him: Master, what shall we do? He said to them: Do nothing more than what is appointed to you.
Then the soldiers asked him and said: What shall we do? And he said to them: Do not strike anyone or do anyone harm, and be content with your wages.

As the people were waiting in expectation and all were wondering in their hearts about John, whether perhaps he might be the Christ, the Jews sent priests and deacons from Jerusalem to ask him: Who are you? And he confessed and did not deny it, and he confessed that he was not the Christ.
Then they asked him: What then, are you Elijah? And he said: I am not. Are you the prophet? And he answered: No.

Then they said to him: Who are you, then? Tell us, so that we may give an answer to those who sent us. What do you say about yourself? He said: I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord, as Isaiah the prophet said. And those who had been sent were from the Pharisees.
Then they asked him and said: Why do you baptize, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the prophet?

Then John answered them, saying thus: I baptize you in water for repentance; but he who is coming after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to carry. In your midst stands one whom you do not know; he will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and in fire.
His winnowing shovel is in his hand, and he will clean out his threshing floor and gather his wheat into his barn; the chaff he will burn in unquenchable fire.
He preached the gospel to the people with many other exhortations as well. These things happened in Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
Then Jesus came into Galilee and to the Jordan, to John, to be baptized by him. Jesus himself was about thirty years old when he began, and people supposed he was the son of Joseph.

But John tried to prevent him, saying: "I ought to be baptized by you, and you come to me?" Then Jesus answered and said to him: "Let it be so now; this is how it is fitting for us to fulfil all righteousness." Then he let him.
Then it happened that when all the people had been baptized, and Jesus had been baptized and was praying, he came up at once out of the water.
And behold, the heavens were opened to him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending in bodily form like a dove and coming upon him.
And behold, a voice said from heaven: "You are my beloved Son; in you I am well pleased."
And John bore witness, saying: "I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove, and it remained upon him. I did not know him, but the one who sent me to baptize in water said to me:
'The one on whom you see the Spirit descending and remaining is the one who baptizes in the Holy Spirit.' And I have seen and borne witness that this is the Son of God."
Then Jesus was led by the Spirit into the desert to be tempted by the devil.
And when he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he was hungry afterwards.

Then the tempter came to him and said to him: "If you are the Son of God, say that these stones should become bread." Then he answered and said: "It is written that man does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God."

Then the devil took him into the holy city and set him on the highest roof of the temple and said to him: "If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here. It is written that he will command his angels concerning you, and they will take you up in their hands so that you do not strike your foot against a stone." Then Jesus said to him: "It is also written that you shall not tempt the Lord your God."

Again the devil took him up onto a very high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the earth and their glory, and said to him: "All these I will give you, if you fall down and worship me." Then Jesus said to him: "Go away, Satan! It is written that you shall worship the Lord your God and serve him alone."
And when all the temptation was finished, the devil left him for a time. He was then among the wild beasts, and angels of God came to him and served him.
On the next day John was standing there again with two of his disciples, and he saw Jesus walking and said: "Behold the Lamb of God! Behold, this is the one who takes away the sin of the world!"

Then the disciples heard him speaking, and they followed Jesus. Jesus turned and saw them following him, and said to them: "What are you looking for?" They said to him: "Rabbi" (which means "master"), "where do you live?" He said to them: "Come and see." So they came and saw where he lived, and they stayed with him that day. It was then the tenth hour of the day.
One of them was Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter. He was one of the two who had heard the words from John and were following him.

He first found his brother Simon and said to him: "We have found the Messiah" (which means "Christ"). And he led him to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said: "You are Simon, son of John. You are called Cephas" (which means "Peter").
The next morning he wanted to go into Galilee. He found Philip and said to him: "Follow me." Philip was from Bethsaida, the town of Andrew and Peter.
And Philip found Nathanael and said to him: "We have found the one Moses wrote about in the law, and the prophets wrote about too: Jesus, son of Joseph, from Nazareth."
Then Nathanael said to him: "Can anything good come from Nazareth?" Philip said to him: "Come and see."
Jesus saw Nathanael coming to him and said of him: "Here is a true Israelite, in whom there is no deceit."
Then Nathanael said to him: "How do you know me?" Jesus answered and said to him: "Before Philip greeted you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you."

Then Nathanael answered him and said to him: "Master, you are the Son of God, you are the King of Israel." Then Jesus answered him and said to him: "You believe because I told you I saw you under the fig tree. You will see greater things than these."
And he said to him: "Truly I tell you, you will see heaven opened, and the angels of God going up and coming down upon the Son of Man."
And Jesus then returned in the power of the Spirit into Galilee, and a report about him went out through the whole region. He taught in their synagogues and was praised by everyone.
Then he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up. As was his custom, he went into the synagogue on the sabbath day and stood up to read, and he was handed the book of the prophet Isaiah.

When he opened the book, he found the place where it was written: "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me. He has sent me to bring the good news to the poor, to proclaim release to captives and sight to the blind, to set the broken free, to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord and the day of retribution."
And when he had closed the book, he gave it to the attendant and sat down, and the eyes of everyone in the synagogue were fixed on him.
Then he began to say to them: "Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing."
From then on Jesus began to preach, saying: "The time is fulfilled. Repent and believe the gospel, for the kingdom of heaven is now drawing near."
Walking by the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting their nets into the sea, for they were fishermen.
And he said to them: "Come after me, and I will make you fishers of men." At once they left their nets and followed him.

Going on further from there, he saw two other brothers, James the son of Zebedee and John his brother, in a boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets, and he called them. At once they left their nets and their father and followed him.

Then it happened, while the crowds were pressing upon him to hear the word of God, that he was standing by the Lake of Gennesaret, and he saw two boats standing by the lake. The fishermen had gone down from them to wash their nets.
He got into one of the boats, which was Simon's, and asked him to take it out a little from the land. Then he sat down and taught the crowd from the boat.

When he had finished speaking, he said to Simon: "Push the boat out into the deep, and let down your nets for a catch." Then Simon answered and said to him: "Master, we worked all this night and caught nothing, but at your word I will let down the net."

When they had done this, they caught a great quantity of fish, and their net was breaking. They signalled to their partners who were in the other boat to come and help them. They came and filled both boats, so that they were sinking.

When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at the knees of the Saviour and said: "Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, Lord." Fear had seized him and all who were with him at the catch of fish that they had taken, and likewise James and John, the sons of Zebedee, since they were Simon's partners.

Then the Saviour said to Simon: "Do not be afraid; from now on you will catch men." Then his disciples believed in him, and when they had brought the boats to land, they left everything and followed him.
As the Saviour went on from there, he saw a man called Matthew sitting at the tax booth, and said to him: "Follow me."
Then he rose up, left everything, and followed him.
After this the Saviour and his disciples came into the land of Judea, and there he stayed with them and baptized.
John too was baptizing at Aenon near Salim, because there was much water there, and people came to him and were baptized. John had not yet been put in prison.
Then a dispute arose between John's disciples and the Jews about purification.
And they came to John and said to him: "Master, the one who was with you beyond the Jordan, to whom you bore witness, look, he is baptizing here, and everyone is coming to him."
Then John answered and said: "A man cannot receive anything unless it is given to him from heaven. You yourselves bear me witness that I said: I am not the Christ, but I have been sent before him."

He who has the bride is the bridegroom; but the friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly at the voice of the bridegroom. So this joy of mine is fulfilled. He must increase, and I must decrease.

He who came from above is above all. He who is from the earth is of the earth and speaks of the earth. He who came from heaven is above all, and he testifies to what he has seen and heard, yet no one accepts his testimony. Whoever has accepted his testimony has certified that God is true. The one whom God sent speaks the word of God, for God does not give him the Spirit by measure.
Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life; whoever does not believe the Son will not see life, but the wrath of God remains on him.
So when Jesus then learned that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was making and baptizing more disciples than John — although Jesus himself did not baptize, but his disciples did —
and that John had been handed over, he then left Judea and went back into Galilee.
When he heard that John had been handed over, he went into Galilee. Leaving the town of Nazareth, he came and lived in Capernaum by the sea, in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali,

so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled: "Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the way of the sea beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles: the people who sat in darkness have seen a great light, and for those who sat in the region of the shadow of death a light has dawned."
And Jesus went about all of Galilee, teaching in their synagogues and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and every infirmity among the people.

And his fame spread into all of Syria, and they brought to him all who were sick, those afflicted with various diseases and seized by torments, and those who had devils, and lunatics and paralytics, and he healed them.
And great crowds followed him from Galilee and from the Decapolis and from Jerusalem and from Judea and from beyond the Jordan.
And they held him back so that he would not leave them. Then he said to them: "I must preach the kingdom of God to the other towns as well, for that is why I was sent."
When he saw the crowds, he went up onto a mountain. When he had sat down, he called to him those whom he wanted, and they came to him. And he appointed twelve to be with him, whom he named apostles:

Simon, whom he called by another name, Peter; and Andrew his brother; and James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James, to whom he gave the name Boanerges, which means "sons of thunder"; Philip and Bartholomew, Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon, who is called the Zealot; and Judas the brother of James, and Judas, called by another name Iscariot, who was the betrayer.
And then his disciples came to him, and lifting up his eyes toward them, he opened his mouth and taught them, saying:
"Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of God.
Blessed are the meek, for they will possess the earth.
Blessed are those who weep, for they will be comforted.
Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be filled.
Blessed are those who are merciful, for they will obtain mercy.
Blessed are those who are pure in heart, for they will see God.
Blessed are those who are peaceable, for they will be called children of God.
Blessed are those who suffer persecution for the sake of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

Blessed are you when people curse you and hate you and persecute you and, lying, say every evil against you; when they cut you off and reproach you and cast out your name as evil for the sake of the Son of Man.
Rejoice on that day and be glad, for your reward is abundant in heaven.
For so their fathers persecuted the prophets who were before you.
But woe to you who are rich, for you have your comfort.
Woe to you who are filled, for you will hunger.
Woe to you who laugh now, for you will weep and mourn.
Woe to you when all people speak well of you: for in the same way their fathers did to the false prophets.
But to you who hear, I say: you are the salt of the earth.
If the salt loses its savour, with what will it then be salted?
It is no longer good for anything, except to be thrown out and trodden underfoot by people.
You are the light of the world. A city set on a mountain cannot be hidden.
Nor do people light a lamp and put it under a bushel, or under a bed, or in a hidden place, or under a vessel, but on a lampstand, so that it gives light to all who are in the house.
In the same way let your light shine before people, so that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
Do not think that I have come to abolish the law or the prophets; I have not come to abolish but to fulfil.
Truly I tell you: until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota or one stroke will pass from the law until all these things come to pass.

Whoever breaks one of the least of these commandments and teaches people so will be called least in the kingdom of heaven. But whoever does them and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
I tell you: unless your righteousness is more abundant than that of the scribes and the Pharisees, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven.
You have heard that it was said to the people of old: You shall not be a killer; whoever kills is liable to judgement.
But I tell you that everyone who is angry with his brother is liable to judgement.
Whoever says to his brother, 'Empty one!', is liable to the council.
Whoever says, 'Fool!', is liable to the fire of hell.

If you bring your gift to the altar, and there you then remember that your brother has something against you, then leave your gift there before the altar; go first to be reconciled with your brother, and then come and bring your gift.

Be quick to come to terms with your adversary while you are on the way with him, lest perhaps your adversary hand you over to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and then you are sent into prison.
Truly I say to you: you will not go out from there until you pay the last coin.
You have heard that it was said to the ancients: 'Do not commit adultery.' I say to you that everyone who looks at a woman to desire her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
If your right eye causes you to sin, pluck it out and throw it away from you: it is better for you that one of your members perish than that your whole body be sent into the fire of hell.
And if your right hand causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away from you: it is better for you that one of your members perish than that your whole body go into the fire of hell.
It has been said: whoever dismisses his wife, let him give her a bill of divorce.
But I say to you that everyone who dismisses his wife, except on account of fornication, causes her to commit adultery; and whoever marries the dismissed woman commits adultery.
You have heard that it was said to the ancients: 'Do not swear falsely, for you shall render to God your false oaths.'
But I say to you that one should not swear at all: neither by heaven, for it is God's throne;
nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of his feet; nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great king.
Nor shall you swear by your head, for you cannot make one hair of your head white or black.
Let your word be: 'It is, it is'; 'It is not, it is not.' Whatever is beyond that is from evil.
You have heard that it was said: 'An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.'
But I say to you that you should not resist evil.
But if anyone strikes you on your right cheek, offer him the other.
And to him who wants to quarrel with you in strife and take your tunic, let him have the cloak as well.
And whoever compels you to go a thousand paces with him, go with him another two.
Whoever asks something of you, give to him; and whoever wants to borrow from you, do not refuse him.
And whoever takes the things that are yours, do not ask for them back.
As you wish people to do to you, so you also do to them.
You have heard that it was said: 'Love your neighbour and hate your enemy.'
I say to you: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who persecute and harm you.
That you may be children of your Father who is in heaven, who makes the sun rise over the evil and over the good, and sends rain over the just and over the unjust.
If you love those who love you, what reward will you have then? Do not the wicked men [publicans] do that?
And if you do good to those who do good to you, what thanks is due to you for that? Sinful men do that.
If you lend to those from whom you hope to receive repayment, what thanks is due to you then? Even sinful men lend to sinful men, so that they may receive the same back.
And if you greet only your brothers, do not heathen men do that?

But rather, love your enemies and do good to them, and lend, hoping for nothing in return, and your reward will be great, and you will be children of the Most High, for he is gracious toward the ungrateful and the evil.
Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
Be perfect, just as your heavenly Father is perfect.
Take care that you do not do your righteous deeds before men in order to be seen by them; otherwise you will have no reward with your Father who is in heaven.

When you give alms, do not have trumpets sounded before you, as the hypocrites do in the assemblies and in the villages, so that they may be honored by men. Truly I say to you: they have received their reward.
When you give alms, let your left hand not know what your right hand is doing, so that your alms may be in secret; and your Father, who sees it in secret, will repay you.

When you pray, do not be like the hypocrites, who love to pray standing in the synagogues and at the street corners, so that they may be seen by men. Truly I tell you: they have received their reward.
But when you pray, go into your chamber, shut your door, and pray to your Father in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will then repay you.
When you pray, do not try to speak much, as the heathen do: they think that they will be heard because of their many words.
Truly, do not try to be like them: your Father knows what you need before you ask him.
Then one of his disciples said to him: Lord, teach us to pray, as John taught his disciples.

Then he said to them: When you pray, say this: Our Father, you who are in heaven, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done, as it is in heaven, so may it be here on earth. Give us today our daily bread, and forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors, and do not lead us into temptation, but deliver us from evil.
If you forgive men their sins, then your heavenly Father will forgive you your sins. If you do not forgive men, then your Father will not forgive you your sins.
When you fast, do not try to be gloomy like the hypocrites: they disfigure their faces so that they may show men that they are fasting. Truly I say to you that they have received their reward.
When you fast, anoint your head and wash your face, so that you are not seen by people to be fasting, but only by your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will repay you.
Do not be afraid, little flock, for it has pleased your Father to give you the kingdom.
Sell what you have in possession and give alms; make yourselves purses that do not grow old, a treasure that does not fail, in heaven.

Do not store up for yourselves treasure on earth, where rust and moth destroy it; store up for yourselves treasure in heaven, where neither rust nor moth destroys it, and thieves do not dig through or steal.
Where your treasure is, there your heart is.
The lamp of the body is the eye. If your eye is clear, then your whole body is full of light; if your eye becomes corrupt, then your whole body is dark.
If the light that is in you is darkness, how great is that darkness?
No one can serve two lords: either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will hold to the one and despise the other.
You cannot serve God and worldly wealth.
Therefore I say to you: do not be anxious about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will clothe it with. Surely life is more than food, and the body more than clothing.
Look at the birds of heaven: they do not sow or reap or gather into barns, and your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not worth more than they are?
Which of you by thinking can add one ell to his stature? If you cannot do what is least, why then are you anxious about the rest? And why are you anxious about clothing?
Look at the lilies of the field, how they grow; they do not labor or spin. I say to you that Solomon in all his glory was not clothed like one of these.
If God so clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, how much more will he clothe you, you of little faith?
Do not be anxious, saying: What shall we eat, or what shall we drink, or what shall we clothe ourselves with? The Gentiles seek all these things. Your Father knows that you need all of this.
Seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you.
Do not be anxious about tomorrow: tomorrow will take care of itself. Each day has enough trouble of its own.
Do not judge, so that you are not condemned; as you judge in judgment, so you will be judged.
Do not condemn, so that you are not condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven.
Give, and it will be given to you: a good measure, filled, shaken down, and overflowing, will be poured into your lap.
The measure you measure with is the measure that will be measured to you.
Why do you see the speck in your brother's eye and not see the beam in your own eye? Or how can you say to your brother, 'Let me take the speck out of your eye,' when there is a beam in your own eye?
Hypocrite, first cast the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see to cast the speck out of your brother's eye.
Do not give what is holy to dogs, nor cast your pearls before swine, lest perhaps they trample them under their feet, and turn and tear you to pieces.
Which of you has a friend and goes to him at midnight and says to him: 'Friend, lend me three loaves, for a friend of mine has come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him.'
And he from within should answer: 'Do not trouble me; my doors are already shut, and my servants are with me in the chamber; I cannot get up and give to you.'
I say to you: even if he will not get up and give to him because he is his friend, yet because of his persistence he will get up and give him as much as he needs.
And I say to you: ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks receives, and whoever seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.
Or which man among you, if his son asks for bread, will give him a stone? If he asks for a fish, will he then give him a snake? Or if he asks for an egg, will he then give him a scorpion?
If you, then, although you are evil, know how to give good things to your children, how much more will your Father who is in heaven give good things to those who ask him?
Whatever you wish people to do to you, do the same to them; that is the law and the prophets.
Enter through the narrow gate, for wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many are those who go through it.
How narrow is the gate and how constricted the way that leads to life! And few are those who find it.
Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves.
By their fruits you will know them.
Do people gather grapes from thorns, or figs from thistles? So every good tree bears good fruit, and a bad tree bears bad fruit.
A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, nor can a bad tree bear good fruit.
A good man brings forth good out of the good treasure of his heart, and an evil man brings forth evil out of the evil treasure.
Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.
Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
Truly, by their fruits you will know them.
Not everyone who says to me, 'Lord, Lord!' will enter the kingdom of heaven; but whoever does the will of my Father who is in heaven, he will enter the kingdom of heaven.
Many will say to me on that day: 'Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, and in your name cast out devils, and in your name do many mighty works?'
Then I will declare to them: 'Because I never knew you, depart from me, you who work iniquity!'

Everyone who hears these words and does them is like a wise man who built his house on rock; and the rain came down, and the floods came, and the winds blew and beat upon that house, and it did not fall, because it was founded on rock.

And everyone who hears these words of mine and does not do them is like a foolish man who built his house on sand. The rain came down, the floods came, the winds blew and beat against that house, and it fell, and great was its fall.
When the Savior had finished these words, the crowds were amazed at his teaching.
For he was teaching them as one who had authority, and not as the scribes and Pharisees.
Then, seeing the crowds, he had compassion on them, because they were harassed and lying like sheep that have no shepherd.
And he called his twelve disciples to him and gave them power over unclean spirits, to cast them out and to heal every sickness and every infirmity.

And he sent them to preach the kingdom of God, and said to them: Take nothing with you on the way. Do not go on the road of the Gentiles, and do not go into the cities of the Samaritans, but go rather to the sheep of the house of Israel that are lost.
As you go, preach, saying: The kingdom of heaven is drawing near.
Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse lepers, cast out devils. You received without payment; give without payment.
Do not seek to have gold or silver or money in your belts, nor a bag for the journey, nor bread, nor two tunics, nor shoes, nor a staff. The worker is worthy of his food.
Whatever city or town you enter, ask who in it is worthy, and stay there until you leave, eating and drinking what they set before you. Heal the sick who are in it, and do not go from house to house.
When you enter the house, greet it, saying: Peace be to this house! If the house is worthy, your peace will come upon it; if it is not worthy, your peace will return to you.
And whoever does not receive you or hear your words, when you go out of that house or that city, shake the dust off your feet as a testimony against them.
Truly I say to you: it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that city.
Behold, I am sending you out like sheep in the midst of wolves: be wise as serpents and pure as doves.

Beware of men: they will hand you over to their councils and scourge you in their synagogues, and you will be brought before governors and kings for my sake, as a testimony to them and to the Gentiles.

When they hand you over to synagogues, magistrates and authorities, do not be anxious about how or what you will answer or what you will say. What you are to speak will be given to you in that hour. For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father speaks in you.

Brother will hand over brother to death, and the father his son, and children will rise up against their parents and have them put to death, and you will be hated by all for my name's sake. Whoever endures to the end will be saved.
When they persecute you in this city, flee to another. I tell you truly: you will not have gone through all the cities of Israel before the Son of Man comes.

The disciple is not above the master, nor the servant above his lord. It is enough for the disciple that he be like his master, and the servant like his lord. If they called the father of the household Beelzebub, how much more will they call his household so?
Do not fear them: nothing is covered that will not be uncovered, and nothing is hidden that will not be known.
What I say to you in darkness, say in the light; what you have heard in your ears, preach on the rooftops.
I say to you, my friends: do not fear those who kill the body, for they cannot kill the soul; but rather fear him who can destroy both soul and body in the punishment of hell.

Look now, are not two sparrows bought for a coin? And not one of them falls to the earth without your Father. The hairs of your head are all numbered. Do not be afraid: you are better than many sparrows.

Everyone who confesses me before men, I will confess him before my Father who is in heaven and before his angels. Whoever denies me before men and is ashamed of me in this adulterous and sinful generation, I will deny him before my Father who is in heaven and his angels, and the Son of Man will put him to shame when he comes in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.

Do not think that I came to send peace on earth: I did not come to send peace, but a sword. From now on five in one house will be divided: three against two and two against three will be divided. I came to set a man against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law, and a man's enemies will be the members of his own household.
Whoever loves his father and mother more than me is not worthy of me, and whoever loves son or daughter above me is not worthy of me.
And whoever does not take up his cross and follow me is not worthy of me, nor can he be my disciple. Whoever finds his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for my sake will find it.
And whoever receives you receives me, and whoever receives me receives him who sent me.
Whoever receives a prophet in the name of a prophet will receive the reward of the prophet.
And whoever gives one of these least ones a cup of cold water to drink, only in the name of a disciple, because you belong to Christ, truly I say to you, he will not lose his reward.
Then it happened, when Jesus had finished giving commands to his twelve disciples, that he went on from there to teach and preach in their cities.
The disciples went out and preached that people should repent, and they cast out many devils, and anointed many sick people with oil and healed them.
On the third day a wedding was held in the place called Cana of Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there. Jesus and his disciples had also been invited there to the wedding.
When the wine had run out, the mother of Jesus said to him: "They have no wine." Then Jesus said to her: "What is that to you and to me, woman? My hour has not yet come."
Then his mother said to the servants: "Do whatever he tells you."
Six stone water jars were set there for the purification rites of the Jews. Each of them could hold two or three measures.
Then the Savior said to them, "Fill the jars with water." And they filled them to the brim.
Then the Savior said to them, "Now draw some out and take it to the steward of the feast." And they took it.

The steward tasted the water that had been turned into wine. He did not know where it had come from, though the servants who had drawn the water knew. Then the steward called the bridegroom and said to him, "Everyone serves the good wine first, and when the guests are drunk, then the worse. You have kept the good wine until now."
The Savior did this, the first of his signs, in the place called Cana of Galilee, and he revealed his glory.
When he came down from the mountain, great crowds followed him.
Then a man with leprosy came, knelt down and worshipped him, saying, "Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean."
The Savior stretched out his hand and touched him, saying, "I am willing. Be clean!" And at once his leprosy was healed.
Then the Savior said to him, "See that you tell no one. But go and show yourself to the priest, and bring the offering that Moses commanded, as a testimony to them."

But he went out and began to preach and spread the news, so that the Savior could no longer go openly into the town. Instead he stayed outside in deserted places, and people came to him from everywhere.
When he went into Capernaum, a centurion came to him and pleaded with him,
saying, "Lord, my servant is lying paralyzed at home and is suffering terribly."
Then the Savior said to him, "I will come and heal him."
The centurion answered, "Lord, I am not worthy for you to come under my roof. Just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
I am a man under authority myself, with soldiers under me. I say to one, 'Go,' and he goes, and to another, 'Come,' and he comes, and to my servant, 'Do this,' and he does it."
When the Savior heard this, he was amazed and said to those who were following him, "Truly I tell you, I have not found such great faith in Israel.

I tell you that many will come from the east and the west and sit down with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven. But the children of this kingdom will be thrown out into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth."
Then the Savior said to the centurion, "Go. Let it be done for you as you have believed." And the servant was healed at that very hour.
Then the centurion returned to his house and found that the servant who had been sick was healed.
When the Savior came into Peter's house, he saw Peter's mother-in-law lying in bed with a fever.
He touched her hand, and the fever left her. Then she got up and served them.
After this he went to a town called Nain, and his disciples and a large crowd went with him.
When he then came near the gate of the city, behold, a dead man was being carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow; and a great crowd from the city was with her.
When the Lord saw her, he was moved with compassion for her and said to her: "Do not weep!" And he went up and touched the bier.
Those who were carrying it stood still, and he said: "Young man, I say to you, arise!" And he who had been dead sat up and began to speak, and he gave him to his mother.
Then fear seized them all, and they glorified God, saying: "A great prophet has arisen among us," and, "God has visited his people."
And this word about him went out into all Judea and all the surrounding region.
When evening had come, they brought to him many who had devils, and he cast out the spirits with a word and healed all who were sick.
This was so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, who said: "He took on our infirmities and bore our diseases."
Then Jesus saw a great crowd around him, and he commanded that they cross over to the other side of the sea.
Then a scribe came up and said to him: "Master, I will follow you wherever you go."
Then Jesus said to him: "Foxes have holes, and the birds of heaven have nests where they rest, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head."

Then he said to another man: "Follow me!" He said to him: "Lord, let me first go and bury my father." Then Jesus said to him: "Follow me, and let the dead bury their dead. You go and proclaim the kingdom of God!"

Then another said: "I will follow you, Lord, but first let me say farewell to those who are at home." Then Jesus said to him: "No one who puts his hand to the plough and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God."
As he got into a boat, his disciples followed him.
And then a great storm arose on the sea, so that the boat was covered by the waves.
He, however, was in the boat, sleeping on a pillow.
Then they came to him and woke him, saying: "Lord, save us, for we are perishing!"
Then he said to them: "Why are you afraid, you of little faith?"
Then he got up and rebuked the wind and the sea, and said: "Be silent and be still!" Then there was a great calm.
Then the men were amazed, saying among themselves: "Who, or what kind of man, is this, who commands the winds and the sea, and they obey him?"
When he came across the sea into the region of the Gerasenes, which is opposite Galilee,
and when he went out onto land, two men who had devils ran to meet him, coming out of the tombs. They were very fierce, so that no one could pass along that road.
One had had devils in him for a long time already. He did not wear any clothing, and he did not live in a house but in the tombs.
No one could bind him any longer, even with chains, for he had often been bound with fetters and chains, but he had broken the chains and smashed the fetters, and no one could tame him.
And always, night and day, he was in the mountains, crying out and cutting himself with stones.

When he saw Jesus from afar, he ran toward him and worshipped him, and crying out with a loud voice he said: What is there between us and you, Jesus, Son of the highest God? Have you come before the time to torment us?
Then Jesus said to him: Go out, you unclean spirit! Say what your name is. He then said: Multitude, because many devils had gone into him.
And they begged him not to drive them out of the region, and not to command them to go into the abyss.
Not far from them there was a herd of many swine feeding. The devils begged him, saying: If you cast us out, send us into the herd of swine. Then he said to them: Go.
Then they went out and went into the swine, and with great violence the herd, two thousand of them, was hurled down into the lake, and they were drowned in the lake.
Those who fed them fled and told it in the cities and in all the fields.

Behold, then the whole city went out to meet Jesus. And when they saw him, and the man from whom the devils had gone out sitting at his feet, clothed and of sound mind, they were afraid, and they begged him to depart from their borders.
When he then went up into the boat, the man from whom the devils had gone out begged him that he might be with him; and he did not permit him, but said to him:

Go into your house to your own people and tell what the Lord has done for you and how he has had mercy on you. Then he went preaching in the region of the ten cities what Jesus had done for him, and all marveled.

Then he got into a little boat and crossed over and came into his own city. Behold, four men carrying on a bed a man who was lame sought to bring him in and set him before Jesus. When they did not find any way by which they might bring him in through the crowd, they climbed up onto the roof, and through the roof tiles they let him down with the bed into the midst before Jesus. When he saw their faith, he said: Believe, child; then your sins will be forgiven you! Then the scribes and Pharisees began to think, saying: Who is this who speaks blasphemy? Who can forgive sins but God alone? When Jesus perceived their thoughts, he answered and said to them: Why do you think evil in your hearts? Which is easier, to say: Your sins are forgiven you, or to say: Arise and walk? So that you may know that the Son of Man has power on earth to forgive sins, he said to the lame man: I say to you: arise, take your bed and go into your house! Then he arose at once before them, took up that on which he had lain, and went into his house glorifying God. And fear seized them all, and they glorified
God. And they were filled with fear, saying: We have seen wonders today. They praised God, who had given such power to men.
Then he came again into Cana of Galilee, where he had made the water into wine. There was a certain ruler there, whose son was sick in Capernaum.
When he heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee, he went to him and begged him to come down and heal his son, who was then at the point of death.
Then the Savior said to him: Unless you see signs and wonders, you do not believe.
Then the official said to him: Lord, come down before my son dies. Then the Savior said to him: Go, your son lives.
The man believed the word that the Savior had spoken to him, and went.
As he was already going down, servants ran to meet him and told him, saying that his son was alive.
Then he asked them the hour at which he had grown better, and they said to him: Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him.
Then the father understood that it was the hour at which the Savior had said to him: Your son lives. Then he believed, and all his household.
Levi made a great feast for him in his house.
Then it happened, as he sat in the house, behold, many tax collectors and sinners came and sat with the Savior and with his disciples; there were many who followed him.
Then the scribes and Pharisees saw that he ate with the sinners and the tax collectors, and they said to his disciples: Why does your master eat and drink with the tax collectors and the sinners?

When the Savior heard that, he said to them: Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick. Go and learn what this means: I desire mercy, not sacrifice. I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners, to repentance.
Then they said to him: Why do the disciples of John fast often and offer prayers, and likewise those of the Pharisees, but yours eat and drink and do not fast? Then he said:
Can the children of the wedding fast as long as the bridegroom is with them? Days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them; then they will fast in those days.
Then he told them a parable: No one sews a patch of new cloth onto an old garment; otherwise the new piece pulls its filling away from the old, and the tear becomes worse.
And no one puts new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the new wine bursts the skins and is spilled, and the skins are ruined.
Rather, new wine is to be put into new wineskins, and both are preserved.
No one who drinks old wine immediately wants new, but says: The old is better.
Then some of the scribes and Pharisees answered him, saying: Master, we want to see a sign from you.
Then he answered and said to them: An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah the prophet.
Just as Jonah was in the belly of the whale three days and three nights, so the Son of Man is in the heart of the earth three days and three nights.
The men of Nineveh will rise up in the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at the preaching of Jonah: behold, here is more than Jonah!

The queen of the south will rise up in the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon: behold, here is more than Solomon! I say to you, many came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and therefore here is more than Solomon.
When the unclean spirit goes out of a person, it goes through dry places, seeking rest, and does not find it.
Then he says: I will return to my house from which I went out. And when he comes, he finds it empty, swept with brooms and adorned.

Then he goes and takes with him seven other spirits worse than himself, and they go in and dwell there, and then the last state of that man is worse than the first. So it will be with this most wicked generation.
Then it happened, while he was saying these things, that a certain woman from the crowd raised her voice and said to him: Blessed is the womb that bore you and the breasts that you sucked!
He then said: Yes indeed, blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and keep it.
While he was still speaking to the crowds, behold, his mother and his brothers stood outside, seeking to speak with him.
Then someone said to him: Behold, your mother and your brothers are standing outside, looking for you.
He then answered the one who spoke to him in this way and said: Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?
He stretched out his hand toward his disciples and said: Behold my mother and my brothers! Whoever does the will of my Father who is in heaven, he is my brother and sister and mother.
While he was saying these things to them, behold, one of the rulers of the synagogue, whose name was Jairus, came up and begged him, saying:
My daughter has just died; but come and lay your hand on her, and she will live. Then the Savior rose and followed him, and so did his disciples.

Then, behold, a woman who had suffered a flow of blood for twelve years, and had endured much from a great many physicians and had spent everything she had, and could not be healed by any of them but rather grew worse,

came up behind him in the crowd and touched the fringe of his garment. For she said within herself: If I touch his garment, I will be healed. And at once the flow of her blood stopped; and she felt in her body that she was healed of that sickness.
And at once the Savior, perceiving it in himself, said: Who touched me?

Then Peter and those who were with him said: Master, these crowds are pressing upon you and crushing you, and you say: Who touched me? Then the Savior said: Someone touched me; I know that power has gone out from me.
And he looked around to see the woman who had done this.
The woman saw that it was not hidden; she came trembling and fell at his feet, and declared before all the people for what reason she had touched him, and how she had been healed at once.
Then he said to her: Daughter, your faith has made you well; go in peace and be healed of your sickness.
While he was still speaking, someone came from the ruler of the synagogue and said to him: Since your daughter is dead, why do you trouble the master any further now?

When the Savior heard these words, he said to the ruler of the synagogue: Do not be afraid; only believe, and she will be well. And he let no one follow him except Peter and James and John, the brother of James.
When he came into the house of the ruler of the synagogue, he saw the pipers and a crowd in uproar, wailing and weeping loudly.
Then he went in and said: "Go away. The girl is not dead; she is sleeping." And they mocked him, because they knew that she was dead.
Then he put them all out. He took the girl's father and mother and those who were with him, and went in to where the girl was lying.
And he took her hand and said to her: "Talitha cumi," which means: "Girl, I say to you, arise!"
And her spirit returned, and the girl got up at once and walked; she was twelve years old.
Then they were all overcome with great fear, and he strictly ordered them that no one should know of it.
Then he ordered that she be given something to eat. And the report of it went out into all that land.
As Jesus went on from there, two blind men followed him, crying out and saying: "Have mercy on us, Son of David!"
When he came to the house, the blind men came to him. Then Jesus said to them: "Do you believe that I can do this for you?" They said to him: "Yes, Lord."
Then he touched their eyes, saying: "Let it be done to you according to your faith!" And their eyes were opened.
Jesus sternly warned them, saying: "See that no one knows of it." But they went out and spread his fame through all that land.
As they were going out, they brought him a mute man who had a devil. When the devil had been cast out, the mute man spoke.
And the crowds marveled, saying: "Never in all time has anything like this been seen in Israel. Can this be the Son of David?"
But the Pharisees said: "This man casts out devils by Beelzebub, the prince of the devils."
When he saw their thoughts, he said to them: "Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and a house divided against itself does not stand.
If Satan is divided against himself, how then will his kingdom stand? It cannot stand, but has come to an end. For you say that I cast out devils by Beelzebub.
If I cast out devils by Beelzebub, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges.
[?] But if I cast out devils by the finger of God, then surely the kingdom of God has come upon you.
Or how can anyone go into a strong man's house and take his goods, in which he trusted, unless he first binds the strong man and then takes his house from him?
Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.

Therefore I say to you: every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven men, but blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven. And whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him; but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit, it will not be forgiven him, either in this world or in the world to come.
Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree bad and its fruit bad; for truly the tree is known by its fruit.
Brood of vipers, how can you speak good things when you are evil? Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.
A good man brings good things out of a good treasure, and an evil man brings evil things out of an evil treasure.
I say to you that for every idle word that people speak, they will render account of it on the day of judgment. By your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.
Then indeed it happened, while they were travelling, that he himself went into a certain small town, and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house.
She had a sister named Mary, who also sat at the Lord's feet and heard his word.
Martha indeed was busy about much serving. She stood up and said: Lord, do you not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her to help me.
Then the Lord answered and said to her: Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things, but one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the best part, which will not be taken away from her.
Indeed, when John heard in prison of the works of Christ, he called two of his disciples, sent them to the Lord, and said: Are you the one who is to come, or should we wait for another?
At that same time he healed many of diseases and afflictions and evil spirits, and to many who were blind he gave sight.

Then he answered and said to them: Go and tell John what you have seen and heard: the blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead rise, the poor have the gospel preached to them. Blessed is he who is not led astray because of me.
As they were going away from there, he began to speak to the crowd about John: What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
What did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft clothing? Look, those who wear costly clothing and live in luxury are in kings' houses.
What did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, more than a prophet. This is the one of whom it is written: Look, I send my angel before your face, who will prepare your way before you.
Truly I say to you, among those born of women there is no greater prophet than John the Baptist; yet whoever is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
And all the people who heard this, and the tax collectors, acknowledged God as just, having been baptized with John's baptism.
But the Pharisees and those who taught the law rejected God's purpose for themselves, not having been baptized by him.
From the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffers violence, and the violent take it by force.
Indeed, all the prophets and the law prophesied until John. If you are willing to accept it, he is Elijah who is to come. Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!
To what shall I compare this generation? It is like children sitting in the street, who call to their companions and say: We sang for you and you did not dance; we mourned and you did not weep.
For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say: He has a devil.
The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say: Look, a glutton and a wine-drinker, a friend of tax collectors and sinners. And wisdom is justified by her children.
Then he began to reproach the cities in which many of his mighty works had been done, because they did not repent.
Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works that have been done in you had been done in Tyre and in Sidon, they would long ago have repented in haircloth and in ashes.
But truly I say to you: it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than for you.

And you, Capernaum, will you not now exalt yourself up to heaven? You will descend down to hell. For if the mighty works that have been done in you had been done in Sodom, perhaps it would have remained until this day.
Yet truly I say to you, it will be more tolerable for the land of the Sodomites on the day of judgment than for you.
When the apostles came to the Savior, they told him all the things they had done and taught.
And he said to them: Come apart into a desert place and rest a little.
For truly those who came there were many, and they did not even have time to eat.
After this the Lord appointed another seventy-two, and sent them two by two before his face into every city and place where he was about to come, and said to them:
He who hears you hears me, and he who despises you despises me; he who despises me despises him who sent me.
Then the seventy-two returned with joy, saying thus: Lord, even the devils are subject to us in your name. Then he said to them:
I saw Satan falling from heaven like lightning.
Behold, I have given you power to tread upon serpents and scorpions and over all the might of the enemy, and nothing shall harm you.
But nevertheless do not rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you; rejoice rather that your names are written in heaven.

In that same hour he rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said: I praise you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and prudent and revealed them to little ones. [?] Father, for so it was pleasing before you.
All things have been handed over to me by my Father: no one knows the Son except the Father, nor does anyone know the Father except the Son and he to whom the Son wishes to reveal it.

And turning to his disciples he said: Come to me, all you who labor and are burdened, and I will refresh you. Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am meek and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls: my yoke is sweet and my burden is light.
If anyone comes to me and does not hate his father and mother and wife and children and daughters and sisters, and even his own life besides, he cannot be my disciple.
And he who does not carry his cross and come after me cannot be my disciple.
Which of you is there who wishes to build a tower and does not first sit down and count the costs that are necessary, to see whether he has enough to complete it?
Lest, after he has laid the foundations and is not able to complete it, all who see it begin to mock him, saying thus: This man began to build and could not finish it.
