Or what king, setting out to wage war against another king, does not first sit down and consider whether he can go with ten thousand against the one who comes against him with twenty thousand? Or else, while the other is still far off, he sends messengers and asks for terms of peace.
So every one of you who does not renounce all that he possesses cannot be my disciple.
Then it happened on the second-first sabbath, as the Savior went through the grainfields, that his disciples, being hungry, plucked the ears of grain and ate them, husking them with their hands.
Some of the Pharisees said to them: Why do you do what is not permitted to you on the sabbath?

Then the Savior answered them and said: Have you not read what David did when he was hungry, and those who were with him, how he went into the house of God and took the bread set before God, and ate it, and gave it to those who were with him, though it was not permitted for him to eat it, but only for the priests? And he said to them:
Or have you not read in the law that on the sabbath the priests in the temple break the sabbath rest and are without blame?
I tell you that something greater than the temple is here. The sabbath was made for man, not man for the sabbath.
Then it happened on another sabbath that he went into the synagogue and taught, and there was a man there whose right hand was withered.
Then the scribes and the Pharisees watched him to see whether he would heal on the sabbath, so that they might find grounds to accuse him.
But he knew their thoughts; then he said to the man who had the withered hand: Get up and stand in the middle! Then he rose up and stood there.
Then the Savior said to them: I ask you whether it is permitted on the sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to destroy it? Then they were silent.
And looking around at them all, he said to the man: Stretch out your hand! And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored, whole like the other.

Then he said to them: Which man among you who has a sheep, if it falls into a pit on the sabbath, will not take hold of it and lift it out? How much better a man is than a sheep! Therefore it is right to do good on the sabbath.
Then they were filled with madness and discussed among themselves what they might do to the Savior.
The Savior, knowing this, went away from there, and many followed him, and he healed them all; he ordered them not to make him known.

This was so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, who said: Behold my servant whom I have chosen, my beloved, in whom my soul is well pleased; I will put my spirit upon him, and he will proclaim judgment to the nations. He will not quarrel or cry out, nor will anyone hear his voice in the streets; a bruised reed he will not break, and smoldering flax he will not quench, until he leads judgment forth to victory; and in his name the nations will trust.
Then it happened in those days that he went up onto a mountain to pray, and he stayed awake all night in prayer to God.

That day it came about that he called his disciples to him, and going out of the house, he sat by the sea. Great crowds gathered to him, so that he got into a boat and sat there, and the whole crowd stood on the shore. He spoke many things to them in parables, saying:
Behold, the sower went out to sow.
As he sowed, some fell along the way and were trodden down, and birds came and ate them.

Others fell on stony ground, where there was not much earth, and they quickly sprang up, because they had no depth of earth. When the sun rose they were scorched, and because they had no roots, they withered away.
Some fell among thorns; then the thorns grew up and choked it.
Others fell on good earth and yielded fruit, some a hundredfold, some sixtyfold, some thirtyfold.
As he said these things, he cried out: Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!
He set another parable before them and said: The kingdom of heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field.
While the men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went away.
When the grass grew and bore fruit, then the tares appeared.
Then the servants went to the master of the household and said to him: Lord, did you not sow good seed in your field? Where then do the tares come from? He said to them: An enemy has done this.
Then the servants said to him: Do you want us to go and gather it out? He said: No, lest while gathering the tares you uproot the wheat along with it.
Let both grow until the harvest. At harvest time I will say to the reapers: Gather the tares first and bind them in bundles to be burned, and gather the wheat into my barn.
He set forth another parable to them, saying: What is the kingdom of God like, and what do I think it resembles, or with what parable shall we compare it?
It is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took and sowed in his garden. It is the smallest of all herbs, and it becomes a tree, so that the birds of heaven come and dwell in its branches.
He spoke another parable to them: The kingdom of heaven is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, until it was all leavened.
All these things the Savior spoke to the crowd in parables. With many such parables he spoke the word to them, as they were able to hear it, and without a parable he did not speak to them.
This was so that what was said through the prophet might be fulfilled, who says: I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden since the making of the world.

Then the disciples came to him and said: Why do you speak to them in parables? He answered and said to them: To you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.
But privately he explained everything to his disciples. Therefore I speak to them in parables, because seeing they do not see, and hearing they do not hear, nor do they understand.

And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Isaiah, which says: Hearing, you will hear and not understand; and seeing, you will see and not perceive. The heart of this people has grown dull, and they have heard heavily with their ears, and they have closed their eyes, lest at some time they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them.
Blessed are your eyes, because they see, and your ears, because they hear.
Truly indeed I say to you: many prophets and righteous men longed to see the things that you see, and did not see them, and to hear the things that you hear, and did not hear them.

Hear, then, the parable of the sower: whenever anyone hears the word of the kingdom and does not understand it, the evil one comes and takes away what was sown in his heart. This is the one who was sown along the path.

The one who was sown on stony ground is the one who hears the word and at once receives it with joy; but he has no root in himself and lasts only for a while. When trouble and persecution come because of the word, he immediately falls away.
The one who was sown among thorns is the one who hears the word, but the cares of this world and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
The one who was sown in good soil is the one who hears the word and understands it and bears fruit, and yields, one a hundredfold, another sixtyfold, and another [?] thirtyfold.
The kingdom of God is like this: as if a man casts seed into the earth, and sleeps and rises night and day, and the seed sprouts and grows while he does not know how.
The earth bears fruit of its own accord: first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear. When the fruit has come forth, at once he puts in the sickle, because the harvest has come.
Then, having sent the crowd away, he went into the house. His disciples came to him and said: Explain to us the parable of the weeds of the field.

He answered and said: The one who sows the good seed is the Son of Man; the field is the world; the good seed are the children of the kingdom; the weeds are the children of the evil one. The enemy who sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of this world; the reapers are angels. Just as the weeds are gathered up and burned in the fire, so it will be at the end of this world.

The Son of Man will send his angels, and they will gather out of his kingdom all causes of sin and those who do wrong, and will cast them into the furnace of fire: there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth. Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Whoever has ears, let him hear.
The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field, which a man finds and hides; and in his joy over it he goes and sells everything he has and buys that field.
Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a man seeking fine pearls. When he had found one precious pearl, he went and sold everything he had and bought it.

Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a net cast into the sea and gathering fish of every kind. When it was full, they drew it out, sat down by the shore, chose the good ones into vessels and threw the bad ones out.
So it will be at the end of the world: angels will go out and separate the wicked from among the righteous, and send them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

"Have you understood all these things?" They said to him, "Yes." He said to them, "Therefore every scribe who is learned in the kingdom of heaven is like a man who is the father of a household, who brings out of his treasure things new and old."
Then it happened, when the Savior had finished these parables, that he went away from there.

And coming into his native country, he taught them in their synagogues, so that they marveled and said, "Where did this man get this wisdom and such mighty powers, which are worked through his hands?"

"Is this not the craftsman's son? Is not his mother called Mary, and his brothers James and Joseph and Simon and Judas? And are not his sisters all with us? Where did this man get all these things?" And they took offense at him.
And he said to them, "Surely you will say this proverb to me: 'Physician, heal yourself. Whatever we have heard was done in Capernaum, do here also in your native country.'"
"Truly I say to you, no prophet is accepted in his own native country and in his own house."
And he did not do many mighty works there because of their unbelief, except that he healed a few sick people by laying his hands on them. And he marveled at their unbelief.

"In truth I say to you, there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the heaven was shut for three years and six months and a great famine came over all the land. And Elijah was sent to none of them except to a woman, a widow, at Zarephath of Sidon."
"And there were many lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, and none of them was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian."

Then all who were in the synagogue were filled with anger when they heard these things. They rose up, threw him out of the city, and led him to the brow of the hill on which their city was built, so that they could throw him down headlong. But he passed through the midst of them and went away.

At that time Herod the tetrarch sent and seized John and bound him in prison because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, because he had married her. John had said to Herod, "It is not lawful for you to have her."
Herodias plotted against him and wanted to kill him, but could not. [He] feared the people, because they held him to be a prophet.
Herod too, though he wanted to kill him, feared him, knowing him to be a righteous and holy man. He kept him safe, and when he heard him he did many things, and he listened to him gladly.
And when a suitable day came, Herod held a feast on his birthday for the chief men, the nobles and the leading men of Galilee.

When the daughter of that same Herodias came in and danced, and it pleased Herod and those sitting with him, the king said to the girl: "Ask of me whatever you wish, and I will give it to you." And he swore to her: "Whatever you ask, I will give you, even [?] half of my kingdom."
When she went out, she said to her mother: "What shall I ask for?" And she said: "The head of John the Baptist."
When she came in at once with haste to the king, she asked him, saying: "I want you to give me at once, on a platter, the head of John the Baptist."
And the king was saddened; yet because of the oath and those who sat there with him, he did not want to grieve her.
And he sent his guard and beheaded John in the prison. And his head was brought on a platter and given to the girl, and she gave it to her mother.
And his disciples came and took his body and buried it in a tomb, and they came and told the Savior.

Then Herod heard the fame of the Savior and of all the things that were done by him, and he was perplexed, because it was said by some that John had risen from the dead, by some also that Elijah had appeared, and by others also that one of the old prophets had risen.
Then Herod said: "I beheaded John; who then is this of whom I hear such things?" And he sought to see him.
When the Savior heard this, he went from there by boat to a desert place apart. When the crowds heard this, they followed him on foot from the towns.
And going out, he saw a great crowd, and he had pity on them and healed their sick.

When evening had come, the Twelve came to him and said to him: "Send these crowds away, so that they may go into the towns and villages round about, turn in there, and find food, because we are here in a desert place."
Then the Savior said to them: "They have no need to go; you give them something to eat."
Then Philip answered him: "Two hundred pennies' worth of bread is not enough for them, for each of them to receive a little."

Then he said to them: "How many loaves do you have?" One of his disciples, Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, said to him: "There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish; but what are these among so many, unless we go and buy food for all these crowds?" He said to them: "Bring them here to me."
And he commanded them to make them sit down in companies on the green grass, and they sat down in groups by hundreds and by fifties.

Then, having taken the five loaves and the two fish, he looked up to heaven and blessed them, and broke them and distributed them to his disciples, and the disciples to the crowds. And they all ate and were filled; they took up the leftovers, twelve baskets full of the fragments. The number of those who ate was five thousand men, besides women and little children.
And at once he commanded the disciples to get into the boat and go ahead of him across the lake to Bethsaida, while he sent the crowds away.

Then when the people saw the sign that he had done, they said that this is truly the prophet who is to come into the world. Then Jesus, when he perceived that they were about to come to seize him and make him king, fled; and having left the crowd, he went up into the mountain alone to pray.
When evening had come, he was there alone. The boat in the middle of the sea was tossed by the waves, for the wind was against them.

In the fourth watch of the night, seeing them toiling, he came to them walking upon the sea, and he meant to pass by them. And when they saw him walking upon the sea, they were troubled, saying that it was a ghost, and they cried out for fear. And at once Jesus spoke to them, saying: "Take courage, it is I; do not be afraid."
Then Peter answered and said: "Lord, if it is you, bid me come to you over these waters." And he said to him: "Come!" And Peter, getting down from the boat, walked upon the water to come to Jesus.

But when he saw the strong wind, he was afraid, and as he began to sink, he cried out, saying: "Lord, save me!" And immediately Jesus stretched out his hand, caught him, and said to him: "You of little faith, why did you doubt?" And when they had gone up into the boat, the wind ceased, and at once the boat was at the land to which they were going.
Those who were in the boat came and worshipped him, saying: "Truly you are the Son of God."

And when they had crossed over, they came into the land of Gennesaret. And when the people of that place recognized him, they sent into all that region and brought to him all who were sick, and they begged him that they might touch even the fringe of his garment; and whoever touched it was healed.

On the next day the crowd that stood on the other side of the sea saw that there was no other boat there except one, and that Jesus had not gone into the boat with his disciples, but his disciples alone had gone away from there.

But other boats came from Tiberias near the place where they had eaten the bread when the Lord gave thanks. When the crowd saw that Jesus was not there, nor his disciples, they got into boats and came to Capernaum seeking Jesus. And when they found him across the sea, they said to him: "Master, when did you come here?"

Jesus answered them and said: "Truly, truly I say to you, you seek me not because you saw signs, but because you ate of the loaves and were filled. Do not work for the food that perishes, but for that which endures to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you; for on him God the Father has set his seal."

Then they said to him: "What shall we do, that we may work the works of God?" Jesus answered and said to them: "This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he has sent." Then they said to him: "What sign do you do, that we may see it and believe you? What do you work? Our fathers ate manna in the desert, as it is written: He gave them bread from heaven to eat."

Then the Savior said to them: Truly, truly I say to you, it was not Moses who gave you bread from heaven, but my Father gives you the true bread from heaven. The bread of God is that which comes down from heaven and gives life to the world. Then they said to him: Lord, give us this bread always.

Then the Savior said to them: I am the bread of life; whoever comes to me will not be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty. But I said to you that you have seen me and do not believe. All that the Father gives me comes to me, and whoever comes to me I will not cast out. For I came down from heaven not to do my own will, but the will of him who sent me. This is the will of the Father who sent me: that of all that he has given me I lose nothing, but raise it up on the last day. This is the will of my Father who sent me: that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him should have eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day.

Then the Jews murmured about him because he said: I am the bread that came down from heaven. And they said: Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How can this man say, I came down from heaven?

The Savior answered and said to them: Do not murmur among yourselves. No one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws him, and I will raise him up on the last day. It is written in the prophets: And they shall all be taught by God. Everyone who has heard from the Father and learned comes to me. Not that anyone has seen the Father, except he who is from God; he has seen the Father.

Truly, truly I say to you: whoever believes in me has eternal life. I am the bread of life. Your fathers ate manna in the desert and died. Here is the bread that comes down from heaven, so that whoever eats of it will not die. I am the living bread that came down from heaven. Whoever eats of this bread will live forever, and the bread that I will give is my flesh, for the life of the world.

Then the Jews argued among themselves, saying: How can this man give us his flesh to eat? Then the Savior said to them: Truly, truly I say to you, unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you do not have life in you. Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day. For my flesh is truly food and my blood is truly drink. Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood dwells in me and I in him. As the living Father sent me and I live through the Father, so whoever eats me will also live through me. This is the bread that came down from heaven: not as your fathers ate manna and died; whoever eats this bread will live forever.

He said these things while teaching in the synagogue in Capernaum. Many of his disciples who heard it said: "This is a hard saying; who can listen to it?" Jesus, knowing in himself that his disciples were murmuring about this, said to them: "Does this offend you [?]? What if you see the Son of Man ascending to where he was before? It is the spirit that gives life; the flesh profits nothing. The words that I have spoken to you are spirit and life. But there are some of you who do not believe." And he said: "This is why I told you that no one can come to me unless it is given to him by my Father."

From then on many of his disciples went back and no longer walked with him. Jesus said to the twelve: "Do you want to go away as well?" Simon Peter answered: "Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life, and we have believed and understood that you are the Christ, the Son of God." Jesus answered them: "Did I not choose you twelve? Yet one of you is a devil." He was speaking of Judas Iscariot, son of Simon, who was going to betray him, although he was one of the twelve.
A certain Pharisee asked him to dine with him. And he went in and sat down at table. The Pharisee, thinking to himself, began to say: "Why did you not wash before the meal?"

And the Lord said to him: "Now you Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but what is inside you is full of robbery and wickedness. Fools! Did not he who made the outside also make the inside? But rather, give what is left over as alms, and behold, everything will be clean for you."

Pharisees and some of the scribes came from Jerusalem. When they saw some of his disciples eating bread with unclean hands, that is, with unwashed hands, they found fault, saying: "Why do your disciples break the tradition of the elders? They do not wash their hands when they eat bread."
He answered them: "Why do you break God's commandment for the sake of your tradition? For God said: Honour your father and mother; and whoever curses his father or mother, let him surely die."

"But you say: whoever says to his father or mother, 'Whatever gift comes from me will benefit you,' and does not honour his father and mother — so you have made God's commandment void for the sake of your tradition."

The Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands often, keeping the tradition of the elders. When they come from the marketplace they do not eat unless they wash. And there are many other things handed down to them to keep: the washing of cups, pitchers, bronze vessels, and beds; and they do many other similar things. So you have made God's commandment void for the sake of your tradition.

"Hypocrites! Isaiah prophesied well about you when he said: 'This people honours me with their lips, but their heart is far from me. In vain they worship me, teaching as doctrines the commandments of men.' Abandoning God's commandment, you hold to the tradition of men."
And he called the crowd to him and said to them: "Listen and understand. It is not what goes into the mouth that defiles a person, but what comes out of the mouth, that is what defiles a person."

Then his disciples came to him and said to him: "Do you know that the Pharisees took offence when they heard this saying?" He answered and said: "Every plant that my heavenly Father has not planted will be uprooted. Leave them alone; they are blind, and leaders of the blind. If a blind man leads a blind man, both fall into the pit."

And when he had gone into the house away from the crowd, Peter asked him: "Explain this parable to us." Then he said: "Are you also still without understanding? Do you not understand? Everything that goes into the mouth goes into the belly and is sent out into the drain. But the things that come out of the mouth come out of the heart, and those are what defile a man."

"For out of the heart come evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornication, thefts, false testimonies, greed, wickedness, deceit, lewdness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, and foolishness. These are what defile a man; but eating with unwashed hands does not defile a man."
He rose and went from there into the region of Tyre and Sidon.
And behold, a heathen woman, a Syrophoenician by race, cried out, saying: "Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David! My daughter is badly tormented by the devil."

Jesus gave her no answer at all. Then his disciples came and asked him, saying: "Send her away, for she is crying out after us." He answered and said: "I was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel."

Then she came and worshipped him, saying: "Lord, help me." He said: "Let the children first be fed. It is not good to take the children's bread and throw it to the dogs." Then she said: "Yes [?], Lord, for the whelps eat of the crumbs that fall from their masters' table." Then he said to her: "Woman, great is your faith; let it be done for you as you wish." And her daughter was healed from that hour.

And again, going out from the region of Tyre, he came through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee, through the midst of the region of the Ten Cities. Then they brought to him a man who was deaf and dumb, and asked him to lay his hand on him. He took him aside, away from the crowd, put his fingers into his ears, and, spitting, touched his tongue. Looking up to heaven, he sighed and said to him: "Ephphatha," that is, "Be opened." And immediately his ears were opened and the bond of his tongue was loosed, and he spoke properly.

Then he commanded them to tell no one. But the more he forbade it, the more they proclaimed it, and they marvelled all the more, saying: "He has done all things well; he has made the deaf hear and the dumb speak."

He had to pass through Samaria. So he came to a city of Samaria called Sychar, near the piece of land that Jacob gave to his son Joseph. Jacob's well was there. Jesus, wearied from the journey, sat down just as he was by the well. It was about the sixth hour.

Then a woman from Samaria came to draw water. Jesus said to her: "Give me a drink." (His disciples had gone into the city to buy food.) Then the Samaritan woman said to him: "How is it that you, a Jew, ask a drink of me, a Samaritan woman?" For Jews have no dealings with Samaritans.

Then the Savior answered and said to her: If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who says to you, "Give me to drink," you would perhaps have asked of him that he give you living water. Then the woman said to him: Lord, you have nothing with which to draw, and the well is deep: from where do you have living water? Are you greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well? He drank from it, and his sons and his cattle.

Then the Savior, answering, said to her: Whoever drinks of this water will thirst again; whoever drinks of the water that I give will never thirst, but the water that I give him will be in him a spring of water springing up into eternal life.

Then the woman said to him: Lord, give me that water, so that I may not thirst nor come here to draw. Then the Savior said to her: Go and call your husband and come. The woman answered and said: I have no husband. Then the Savior said to her: You have said well that you have no husband: you have had five husbands, and the one you now have is not your husband: this you have said truly. Then the woman said to him: Lord, I see that you are a prophet. Our fathers worshipped on this mountain, and you say that in Jerusalem is the place where it is fitting to worship. Then the Savior said to her: Woman, believe me, the hour is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem. You worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, for salvation is from the Jews. But the hour is coming, and now is, when the true worshippers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth, for the Father seeks such as worship him. God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and in truth.
Then the woman said to him: I know that the Messiah is coming, who is called Christ: when he comes, he will tell us all things. Then the Savior said to her: I am he, who speak with you.

And then his disciples came quickly, and they wondered why he was speaking with a woman. Yet no one said: What do you seek, or what are you speaking about with her? Then the woman left her water jar and went into the city and said to the people: Come and see the man who told me all the things that I have done; is he not the Christ? Then they went out of the city and came to him.

Meanwhile his disciples asked him, saying: Master, eat. Then he said to them: I have food to eat that you do not know. Then the disciples said among themselves: Has anyone brought him anything to eat? Then the Savior said to them: My food is that I do the will of him who sent me, so that I may accomplish his work. Do you not say that there are yet four months and then the harvest comes? I say to you: lift up your eyes and see the fields, for they are already white for harvest. And he who reaps receives wages and gathers fruit into eternal life, so that he who sows and he who reaps may rejoice together. In this the saying is true: that one is he who sows and another is he who reaps. I sent you to reap that for which you did not labor: others labored, and you have entered into their labor.

From that city many of the Samaritans believed in him through the word of the woman bearing witness to him: "For he told me all the things that I did." When the Samaritans came to him, they asked him to stay there, and he stayed there two days. And many more believed through his word, and they said to the woman: "We no longer believe because of your speech; we ourselves have heard, and we know that this is truly the Savior of the world."

After that there was a feast day of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem. There is in Jerusalem a sheep pool, which is called in Hebrew Bethsaida, having five porches. In them lay a great multitude of the sick, the blind, the lame and the withered, waiting for the stirring of the water. An angel of God at certain times came down into the pool and stirred the water. Whoever stepped in first after the stirring of the water was healed of whatever sickness he was afflicted with.

There was a certain man there who had been thirty-eight years in his infirmity. When Jesus saw him lying there and understood that he had already been so a long time, he said to him: "Do you want to be healed?" Then the sick man answered him: "Lord, I have no one, when the water is stirred, to put me into the pool; while I am coming, another goes down before me."
Then Jesus said to him: "Rise, take up your bed and walk." And at once the man was made whole, and he took up his bed and walked. That day was the Sabbath.

Then the Jews said to the man who had been healed: "It is the Sabbath; it is not lawful for you to carry your bed." Then he answered them: "He who made me whole said to me: Take up your bed and walk." Then they asked him: "Who is the man who said to you: Take up your bed and walk?" But the man who had been healed did not know who it was. For Jesus had slipped away from the crowd that was gathered in that place.

After that Jesus found him in the temple and said to him: "See, you have been made whole; sin no more, so that nothing worse befalls you." The man went and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him whole.

Therefore the Jews persecuted Jesus, because he did these things on the Sabbath. Then Jesus answered them: "My Father is working until now, and I am working." Therefore the Jews sought all the more to kill him, because he not only broke the Sabbath but also called God his Father, making himself equal to God.

Then Jesus answered and said to them: "Truly I say to you: the Son can do nothing of himself, except what he sees the Father doing; whatever things he does, these the Son likewise does. The Father loves the Son and shows him all the things that he does; and he will show him greater works than these, so that you will marvel. For as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so the Son gives life to whom he will. Nor does the Father judge anyone, but he has given all judgment to the Son, so that all may honor the Son as they honor the Father. Whoever does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent him."

Truly, truly I say to you, that whoever hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life and does not come into judgment, but passes from death into life. Truly, truly I say to you, that the hour comes, and now is, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear it will live. As the Father has life in himself, so he has given the Son to have life in himself, and he gave him power to carry out judgment, because he is the Son of Man.

Do not wonder at this, for the hour has come in which all who are in the graves will hear his voice, and they will come forth: those who did good to the resurrection of life, those who did evil to the resurrection of judgment.

I cannot do anything of myself: as I hear, I judge, and my judgment is just. If I bear witness about myself, my witness is not true. There is another who bears witness about me, and I know that the witness he bears about me is true.

You sent to John, and he bore witness to the truth. I do not receive witness from man, but I say these things so that you may be saved. He was a burning and shining light, and you were willing to rejoice for a time in his light.

I have a greater witness than John: the works which the Father gave me to accomplish, the very works that I do, bear witness about me that the Father sent me. And the Father who sent me has himself borne witness about me. You have never heard his voice or seen his form, and you do not have his word dwelling in you, because you do not believe him whom he sent.

Search the scriptures, because you think that in them you have eternal life; and they are the ones that bear witness about me, yet you will not come to me so that you may have life. I do not receive glory from men. But I have known you, that you do not have the love of God in you. I came in my Father's name and you do not receive me; if another comes in his own name, him you receive. How can you believe, you who receive honor from one another and do not seek the honor that comes from the one God? Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father: there is one who accuses you, Moses, in whom you trust. If you believed Moses, you would perhaps believe me, for he wrote about me. If you do not believe his writings, how will you believe my words?

And when he had dismissed him, in those days, when there was again a great crowd, he called his disciples together and said: I have compassion on the crowd, because they have now stayed with me three days and have nothing to eat, and I do not want to send them away fasting, so that they do not collapse on the way. Then the disciples said to him: Where are we to get so many loaves in the wilderness, to satisfy so great a crowd?

Then Jesus said to them: How many loaves do you have? They said: Seven, and a few fish. And he commanded the crowd to sit down on the ground, and taking the seven loaves and the fish and giving thanks, he broke them and gave them to his disciples, and the disciples gave them to the people.
And they all ate and were satisfied; and of the fragments that were left over they took up seven full baskets. Those who ate were four thousand men, besides little children and women.

And he left them, and quickly getting into a boat with his disciples, he came into the region of Dalmanutha. And when his disciples came across the water, they had forgotten to take bread, and they had no more than one loaf with them in the boat. And he warned them, saying: "Look out and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the Sadducees, and of the leaven of Herod." Then they reasoned among themselves, saying: "It is because we have no bread."

Knowing this, the Savior said: "Why do you reason among yourselves, you of little faith, that you have no bread? Do you still not understand, and do you not remember? Are your hearts still blinded? You have eyes but do not see, and you have ears but do not hear, and do you not remember? When I broke five loaves among five thousand, how many baskets full of leftover pieces did you take up?" Then they said to him: "Twelve." "When you divided seven loaves among four thousand, how many baskets of leftover pieces did you take up?" And they said to him: "Seven."

"Why do you not understand that I was not speaking to you about bread when I said, 'Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees'?" Then they understood that he had not told them to beware of the leaven of bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

The Savior came into the region of the city called Caesarea Philippi, and he asked his disciples, saying: "Who do people say that I, the Son of Man, am?" Then they said: "Some say John the Baptist, others say Elijah, and others Jeremiah or one of the prophets."

Then he said to them: "But you, who do you say that I am?" Then Simon Peter answered and said: "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God." Then the Savior answered and said: "Blessed are you, Simon, son of the dove, because flesh and blood did not reveal this to you, but my Father who is in heaven."

"And I say to you that you are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church, and the gates of hell will not prevail against it. And to you I will give the keys of the kingdom of heaven, and whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven." Then he commanded his disciples to tell no one that he was the Savior, the Christ.

From then on the Savior began to show his disciples that he had to go to Jerusalem and suffer many things from the elders, from the scribes, and from the chief priests, and be killed, and rise again on the third day. Then Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him, saying: "Far be it from you, Lord! May this not happen to you!" But he turned and said to Peter: "Get behind me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to me, because you do not understand the things of God, but the things of men."

Then he called the crowd together with his disciples and said to them: "If anyone wants to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me. Whoever wants to save his soul will lose it; whoever loses his soul for my sake will find it. What good is it to a man if he gains the whole world as his possession but suffers the loss of his own soul? Or what will a man give in exchange for his soul?"

The Son of Man is to come in the glory of his Father with his angels, and then he will repay each one according to his work. Truly I say to you, there are some of those standing here who will not taste death before they see the Son of Man coming in his kingdom.

And after six days he took Peter and James and John his brother and led them up a high mountain apart, so that he might pray. And it happened then, while he was praying, that his appearance was changed before them, and his face shone like the sun; his garments became white as snow, exceedingly white and shining, such as no fuller on earth can make white.

Then Moses and Elijah appeared to them, speaking with him in his majesty, and they spoke to him of his departure, which he was to fulfil in Jerusalem. Then Peter answered and said to Jesus: Lord, it is good for us to be here; if you wish, let us make three dwellings here, one for you and one for Moses and one for Elijah.

While he was still speaking, a bright cloud overshadowed them, and behold, a voice from the cloud, saying thus: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear him. And when the disciples heard it, they fell on their faces and were greatly afraid. And Jesus came to them and touched them and said to them: Get up and do not be afraid. Lifting up their eyes, they saw no one but Jesus alone.

And as they were coming down from the mountain, Jesus commanded them, saying thus: Tell no one the vision until the Son of Man rises from the dead. And his disciples asked him, saying thus: Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first? He answered and said to them: Elijah indeed comes and will restore all things.

I say to you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they wished; so too the Son of Man is to suffer at their hands. Then the disciples understood that he was speaking of John the Baptist.

When he came to the crowd, he saw the scribes questioning with them, and at once all the people, seeing him, were astonished and afraid, and running up they greeted him. Then he asked them: What are you disputing among yourselves?

On that same day some of the Pharisees came to him, saying to him: Go out and depart from here, for Herod wants to kill you. Then he said to them: Go and say to that fox: Behold, I cast out devils and accomplish healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I am brought to completion. Nevertheless I must go on today and tomorrow and the following day, for it is not fitting that a prophet should perish outside Jerusalem.

Then it happened on the following day that a man came to him, kneeling down, and cried out, saying: Lord, have mercy on my son, for he is my only one, and he is a lunatic, and an evil spirit seizes him and dashes him down; and he foams and gnashes his teeth and withers and suffers badly, so that he often falls into the fire and often into the water; and suddenly it cries out, and it tears him, and it hardly departs from him, mauling him. And I asked your disciples to cast it out, and they could not heal him.
Then the Saviour answered and said: O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you and bear with you? Bring him to me.

When he came near and saw him, at once the spirit troubled the boy, and, dashed to the ground, he rolled about foaming. And he asked his father: How long is it since this came upon him? He said then: From childhood. If you can do anything, help us, having mercy on us.
Then the Saviour said to him: If you can believe, all things are easy for the one who believes. And crying out, the boy's father said with tears: I believe, Lord; help my unbelief!

And when the Saviour saw the crowd running together, he rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it: You deaf and dumb spirit, I command you, go out of him and never enter into him again! Then, crying out and tearing him, it went out of him, and he became like one dead, so that many said: He is dead.
The Saviour, taking his hand, lifted him up, and he arose, and the boy was healed from that hour. And he gave him back to his father.

Then the disciples came to the Saviour privately and said: Why could we not cast him out? Then the Saviour said to them: Because of your unbelief. Truly I say to you, if you have faith like a grain of mustard seed and say to this mountain: Move from here, it will move, and nothing will be impossible for you. This kind of devils is not cast out except through prayer and fasting.

While they were staying in Galilee, the Saviour said to them: The Son of Man is to be delivered into the hands of men, and they will kill him, and on the third day he will rise again. And they were greatly troubled.

And when they came to Capernaum, those who collected the tribute money came to Peter and said: Does your master not pay the tribute? He said: Yes. And when he went into the house, the Saviour spoke to him first, saying: What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth take tribute or tax, from their own sons or from strangers?

He said then: From strangers. Then the Saviour said to him: Then the sons are free. But so that we do not give them offence, go to the sea and cast your hook, and take the fish that comes up first, and when you open its mouth you will find a coin: take that and give it to them for me and for you.

At that time, when he was in the house, he asked them: What were you discussing on the way? But they were silent, for on the way they had been arguing among themselves about which of them was the greatest.

Then the disciples came to him, saying: Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven? And the Saviour called a little child, set it in the middle of them, and said: Truly I say to you, unless you are turned and become like this little one, you shall not enter the kingdom of heaven.
Whoever humbles himself like this little one is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven. If anyone wishes to be first, he shall be the last of all and the servant of all.

And whoever receives one such little one in my name receives me. Whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him to have a millstone hung around his neck and to be sunk in the depths of the sea.
Then John answered and said: Master, we saw someone casting out devils in your name, and we forbade him, because he does not follow us.
Then the Savior said: Do not forbid him. There is no one who does a mighty work in my name and can soon speak evil of me. Whoever is not against you is for you.
Woe to the world because of offenses! It is necessary that offenses come, but woe to the man through whom the offense comes!

If your hand or your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you. It is better for you to enter into life maimed or lame than to have two hands or two feet and be sent into the eternal fire.

And if your eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it away from you. It is better for you to reign in life with one eye than to have two eyes and be sent into the fire of hell, where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched. Everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be salted with salt.
See that you do not despise one of these little ones. I say to you that their angels in heaven always see the face of my Father who is in heaven. The Son of Man came to save what was lost.

And then he spoke this parable to them, saying: What do you think? If someone has a hundred sheep and one of them goes astray, does he not leave the ninety-nine in the mountains or in the wilderness and go to look for the one that went astray? And if he happens to find it, he lifts it onto his shoulders, rejoicing. And then, coming to his house, he calls together his friends and neighbors and says to them: Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep that was lost.
Truly I say to you, he rejoices over that one more than over the ninety-nine that did not go astray and did not need repentance.
So it is not the will of your Father who is in heaven that one of these little ones should perish.

Or what woman who has ten drachmas, if she loses one drachma, does not light a lamp and sweep the house and search carefully until she finds it? And when she finds it, she calls together her friends and neighbors, saying: Rejoice with me, for I have found the drachma that I lost.
So I say to you: there is joy in heaven before the angels of God over one sinner who repents, more than over ninety-nine righteous people who do not need repentance.

Then he said: A certain man had two sons. The younger of them said to the father: Father, give me the share of the property that falls to me. So he divided the property. Not many days later the younger son gathered everything together and went abroad into a distant country, and there he squandered his property in reckless living.

And after he had lost it all, a severe famine came over that country, and he began to be in want. So he went and attached himself to one of the citizens of that country, who sent him into his fields to feed pigs. And he longed to fill his belly with the pods that the pigs ate, and no one gave him anything.

Then he came to himself and said: "How many hired servants of my father have plenty of bread, and I am perishing here of hunger! I will get up and go to my father and say to him: Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you, and I am no longer worthy to be called your son; make me like one of your hired servants."

And he got up and came to his father. While he was still far off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and running to meet him he fell upon his neck and kissed him. Then the son said to him: "Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you; I am no longer worthy to be called your son."

Then the father said to his servants: "Quickly bring the best robe and clothe him, and put a ring on his hand and shoes on his feet, and bring the fatted calf and kill it, and let us eat and feast, for this son of mine was dead and has come back to life; he was lost and is found." Then they began to feast.

His elder son was in the field, and when he came and drew near to the house, he heard the sound of singing and dancing. And he called one of the servants and asked what these things were. The servant said to him: "Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fatted calf, because he has received him back safe and sound." He was indignant at this and would not go in. His father then came out and began to plead with him.

Then he answered and said to his father: "Look, for so many years I have served you and never transgressed your command, and you never gave me a young goat so that I could feast with my friends; but when this son of yours came, who devoured all his property with harlots, you killed the fatted calf for him."

Then he said to him: "Child, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours. It was fitting to feast and rejoice, for this brother of yours was dead and has come back to life; he was lost and is found."
Take heed to yourselves! If your brother sins against you, go and rebuke him between yourself and him alone. If he listens to you and repents, forgive him, and you have gained your brother.

If he does not listen to you, take with you one or two more, so that every word may stand on the testimony of two or three witnesses. If he does not listen to them, tell it to the assembly; if he does not listen to the assembly, then let him be to you as a heathen and a public sinner.

Truly I say to you, whatever you bind on earth shall be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven. Again I say to you that if two of you agree on earth about any matter, whatever they ask will be done for them by my Father who is in heaven. For where two or three are gathered in my name, there I am in the midst of them.

Then Peter came to him and said: "Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me and I forgive him? Up to seven times?" Then Jesus said to him: "I do not say to you up to seven times, but up to seventy times seven."

Therefore the kingdom of heaven is likened to a man, a king, who wished to settle accounts with his servants. And when he began to settle accounts, one was brought to him who owed ten thousand talents.

Since he had nothing to pay with, the lord commanded that he be sold, along with his wife and children and everything he had, and that payment be made. Then the servant fell down and begged him, saying: "Have patience with me, and I will repay you everything." The lord took pity on the servant, released him and forgave him the debt.

Then the servant went out and found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred pennies, and he seized him and choked him, saying: "Pay what you owe." Then his fellow servant fell down and begged him, saying: "Have patience with me, and I will repay you everything." But he would not; instead he went and had him thrown into prison until he should pay the debt.

When his fellow servants saw what had happened, they were greatly distressed, and they came and told their lord everything that had been done. Then his lord called him and said to him: "Wicked servant, I forgave you all the debt because you begged me. Was it not fitting for you to have pity on your fellow servant, as I had pity on you?"

Then his lord was angry and handed him over to the torturers until he should repay all the debt. And so my heavenly Father will do to you, if each of you does not forgive his brother from your hearts.
And it came to pass that when Jesus had finished these words, he went from Galilee and came into the region of Judea beyond the Jordan, and great crowds followed him, and he healed them there.
And then the Pharisees came to him, testing him, and said: "Is it lawful for a man to put away his wife for any reason at all?"

He answered and said to them: "Have you not read that he who made them in the beginning made them male and female, and said: For this reason a man shall leave father and mother and cleave to his wife, and the two shall be in one flesh? So they are no longer two, but one flesh. What God has joined together, let no man separate."

Then they said to him: "Why then did Moses command that a bill of divorce be given and that she be put away?" Then he said to them: "Because of the hardness of your hearts Moses permitted you to put away your wives; but from the beginning it was not so."

"I say, therefore: whoever puts away his wife, except for fornication, and marries another commits adultery, and whoever marries the woman who has been put away commits adultery." Then his disciples said to him: "If that is how things stand between a man and his wife, then it is not good to marry."

Then he said: "Not all grasp this word, but only those to whom it is given. There are eunuchs who were born so from their mother's womb, and there are eunuchs who were made so by men, and there are eunuchs who have made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. Let whoever can grasp it grasp it."

Then they brought little children to him, so that he would lay his hands on them and pray; his disciples rebuked them. Then Jesus said to them: "Let the little ones be, and do not forbid them to come to me, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these." And when he had laid his hands on them, he went away from there.

Now publicans and many sinners were drawing near to him, to hear him. And the Pharisees and the scribes murmured, saying: This man receives sinners and eats with them. After that Jesus went into Galilee; he would not go into Judea, because the Jews were seeking to kill him.

There were some present at that time who told him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices. Then he answered and said: Do you think that these Galileans were sinners above all the Galileans, because they suffered such things? I do not tell you that; but unless you repent, you will all likewise perish. Just as those eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them: do you think that they were guilty above all the people dwelling in Jerusalem? I do not tell you so; but unless you do penance, you will all likewise perish.

Then he told this parable: A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit on that tree and found none. Then he said to the keeper of the vineyard: Behold, it is now three years since I have been coming to seek fruit on this fig tree, and I find none. Cut it down; why does it occupy the ground in vain? He answered and said to him: Lord, leave it this one year more, until I dig around it and put dung on it, in case it then bears fruit; otherwise, in the future, cut it down.
He was teaching in their synagogue on the sabbath. And behold, there was a woman who had had a spirit of infirmity for eighteen years, and she was bent over and could not look up at all.
When Jesus saw her, he called her to him and said to her: Woman, you are released from your infirmity. And he laid his hand on her, and at once she was made straight and glorified God.

Then the ruler of the synagogue answered, indignant that Jesus had healed on the sabbath, and said to the crowd: There are six days on which it is proper to work; come on those and be healed, and not on the sabbath.
Then Jesus answered and said: Hypocrites, does not each one of you on the sabbath untie his ox or his ass from the manger and lead it to water?

This daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has bound, behold, for eighteen years, was it not proper that she be loosed from this bond on the sabbath? When he said these things, all his adversaries were ashamed, and all the people rejoiced at the things that were gloriously done by him.

Now the feast day of the Jews, the Feast of Tabernacles, was near. Then his brothers said to him: Leave here and go into the land of the Jews, so that your disciples may see the works that you do. For no one does anything in secret while seeking to be known openly; if you do these things, show yourself to the world. For not even his brothers believed in him.

Then Jesus said to them: My time has not yet come, but your time is always ready. The world cannot hate you; it hates me, because I bear witness about it that its works are evil. You go up to this feast day; I am not going up to this feast day, because my time is not yet fulfilled.

When he had said these things, he remained in Galilee. When his brothers had gone up, then he too went up to the feast day, not openly, but as if in secret. The Jews indeed sought him on the feast day and said: Where is he? And there was much murmuring about him in the crowd. Some said: He is good; others said: No, rather he leads the crowd astray. Yet no one spoke openly about him for fear of the Jews.
When the feast day was already half over, the Saviour went up into the temple and taught. And the Jews marvelled, saying: How does this man know letters, since he has not learned them?

Then the Saviour answered them and said: My teaching is not mine, but his who sent me. If anyone wants to do his will, he will understand of the teaching whether it is from God or whether I speak from myself. He who speaks from himself seeks his own glory; but he who seeks the glory of the one who sent him is truthful, and there is no unrighteousness in him. Did not Moses give you the law, and yet none of you keeps the law? Why do you seek to kill me? Then the crowd answered and said: You have a devil; who is seeking to kill you?

Then the Saviour answered and said: I did one work, and you all marvel. Because Moses gave you circumcision (not that it is from Moses, but from the fathers), you circumcise a man on the sabbath. If a man receives circumcision on the sabbath so that the law of Moses is not broken, are you angry with me because I made a whole man healthy on the sabbath? Do not judge according to appearance, but judge a righteous judgement.

Then some from Jerusalem said: Is this not the one whom you seek to kill? And he speaks openly, and they say nothing to him. Can it be that the rulers have truly recognised that this is the Christ? But we know where this man is from; when the Christ comes, no one will know where he is from.

Then the Saviour cried out, teaching in the temple and saying: You both know me and know where I am from; and I have not come of myself, but he who sent me is true, whom you do not know. I know him, because I am from him, and he sent me. And if I say that I do not know him, then I am a liar like you.

Then they sought to seize him, but no one laid his hand on him, because his time had not yet come. Many of the crowd believed in him and said: When the Christ comes, will he do more signs than this man does?

Then someone from the crowd said to him: Master, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me. He then said to him: Man, who appointed me judge or divider over you? Then he said to them: Take heed and beware of all greed, because a person's life does not consist in the abundance of the things he possesses.

Then he told them a parable, saying: A certain rich man's field brought forth abundant fruit. And he thought within himself, saying: What shall I do, since I have nowhere to gather my crops? And he said: This is what I will do: I will tear down my barns and build bigger ones, and there I will gather everything that has grown for me, and my goods. And I will say to my soul: Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years: rest, eat and drink, and feast.
Then God said to him: Fool, this night your soul will be demanded of you; the things you have prepared, whose will they be? So is he who stores up treasure for himself and is not rich in God.

As he was going out on the road, someone ran up ahead and, kneeling before him, asked him, saying: Good master, what good thing shall I do so that I may have eternal life? Then he said to him: Why do you ask me about what is good? No one is good except one, God. If you want to enter into life, keep the commandments.

Then he said to him: Which ones? Then the Saviour said: You shall not kill, you shall not commit adultery, you shall not steal, you shall not bear false witness; honour your father and mother, and love your neighbour as yourself.

Then the young man said to him: All these I have kept since my youth: what do I still lack? Then the Saviour, looking at him, loved him and said to him: One thing you lack: if you want to be perfect, go, sell what you have and give it to the poor, and then you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me. When the young man heard that word, he went away saddened, for he was very wealthy and had many possessions.

And looking around, the Saviour said to his disciples: How hard it is for those who have riches to enter the kingdom of God! Truly I say to you, a rich man will hardly enter the kingdom of heaven. And again I say to you: it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of heaven. When the disciples heard this, they were greatly astonished, saying: Who then can be saved?

Looking at them, the Saviour said to them: With men this is hard; with God all things are easy. Then Peter answered and said to him: Behold, we have left everything and followed you: what then will there be for us? Then the Saviour said to them: Truly I say to you that you who have followed me, in the regeneration, when the Son of Man sits on the throne of his majesty, you too will sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

Truly I say to you: everyone who leaves house or his parents or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or fields for the sake of the kingdom of heaven and my name and for the sake of the gospel will receive a hundredfold: now in this time houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and fields, with persecutions, and in the age to come they will possess eternal life. Many who are first will be last, and the last first.

The Pharisees, who were greedy, heard all these things, and they mocked him. Then he said to them: You are those who justify yourselves before men; God knows your hearts, for what is exalted among men is abominable before God.

Then he said again: There was a certain man who was rich, and he clothed himself in purple and in linen and feasted splendidly every day. And there was a certain poor beggar named Lazarus, who lay at his gate full of sores and longed to be filled with the crumbs that fell from the rich man's table; and the dogs even came and licked his sores.

Then it came to pass that the beggar died and was carried by angels into Abraham's bosom. The rich man also died and was buried in hell. Lifting up his eyes while he was in torment, he saw Abraham far off and Lazarus in his bosom. And he called out and said: Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus to dip the very tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, for I am tormented in this flame.

Then Abraham said to him: Child, remember that you received good things in your life, and Lazarus likewise evil things; now he is comforted and you are tormented. And besides all this, between you and us a great gulf is fixed, so that those who wish to pass from here to you cannot, nor can they cross from there to here. I beg you, father, to send him to my father's house: I have five brothers, so that he may testify to them, lest they also come into this place of torment.

Then Abraham said to him: They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them. Then he said: No, father Abraham, but if someone from the dead goes to them, they will repent. Then he said to him: If they do not hear Moses and the prophets, neither will they believe if someone rises from death.

Then he said to his disciples: There was a certain rich man who had a steward, and this steward was accused to him of squandering his goods. And he called him and said to him: Why do I hear such a reproach about you? Give an account of your stewardship, for you can no longer be steward.

Then the steward said within himself: What shall I do, since my lord is taking my stewardship away from me? I cannot dig, and I am ashamed to beg. I know what I will do, so that when I am put out of the stewardship, they will receive me into their houses.

Then, calling his lord's debtors one by one, he said to the first: How much do you owe my lord? He said: A hundred measures of oil. Then he said to him: Take your bill, sit down quickly, and write fifty. Then he said to another: How much do you owe? He said: A hundred measures of wheat. Then he said to him: Take your bill and write eighty.

And the lord praised the unrighteous steward because he had acted wisely, for the children of this world are wiser in their generation than the children of light. And I say to you: make friends for yourselves by means of the riches of unrighteousness, so that when you fail, they may receive you into eternal dwellings.

He who is faithful in the least is faithful also in the greater; he who is unjust in the little is unjust also in the greater. If you have not been faithful in unrighteous riches, who will entrust to you that which is yours? And if you have not been faithful in what belongs to another, who will give you that which is yours?

The servant who knew his lord's will and did not prepare and did not act according to his will shall be beaten with many [stripes]. He who did not know, and did things deserving [of stripes], shall be beaten with few stripes. From everyone to whom much has been given, much will be sought, and from him to whom they entrusted much, they will demand more.
Do you not know that I came to send fire on the earth? And what do I want, except that it be kindled? I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how troubled I am until it is accomplished!

The kingdom of heaven is like a man, the father of a household, who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard. Having made an agreement with the workers for a day's wage, he sent them into his vineyard. And going out about the third hour, he saw others standing idle in the street. And he said to them: You go into my vineyard too, and I will give you what is right. So they went. He went out again about the sixth and the ninth hour and did the same. About the eleventh hour he went out and found others standing, and he said to them: Why do you stand here idle all day? They said to him: Because no one has hired us. Then he said to them: You go into my vineyard too.

When evening came, the lord of the vineyard said to his steward: Call the workers and pay them their wages, beginning with the last up to the first. When those came who had come about the eleventh hour, they received a penny each. Then the first came, and they thought that they would receive more; they received a penny each. And as they received it, they murmured against the father of the household, saying: These last worked one hour, and you have made them equal to us, who bore the burden of the day and the heat.

He answered one of them and said: Friend, I do you no wrong. Did you not agree with me for a penny? Take what is yours and go. I want to give to this last one the same as to you. Or is it not permitted to me to do what I want? Or is your eye evil because I am good? So the last are first and the first last: many are called, few are chosen.

And it happened, when he went into the house of one of the chief Pharisees on the sabbath to eat bread, that they watched him. And behold, a certain man who had dropsy was before him. Then the Saviour answered and spoke to the lawyers and to the Pharisees, saying: Is it permitted to heal on the sabbath? They were silent. Then he took hold of him, healed him, and let him go.
And then he answered them and said: Which of you, if his ass or ox falls into a pit, will not straightway pull it out on the sabbath day? And they could not answer him to these things.

Then he told a parable to those who had been invited, noticing how they chose the first seats, and said to them: "When you are invited to a wedding, do not sit in the first place, in case someone more honorable than you has been invited by him, and the one who invited you and him comes and says to you, 'Give this man your place,' and then you begin, in shame, to take the last place. But when you are invited, go and sit in the last place, so that when the one who invited you comes, he may say to you, 'Friend, go up higher.' Then you will have honor before those who sit at table with you. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted."

Then he said to the man who had invited him: "When you give a midday meal or an evening meal, do not choose to invite your friends, or your brothers, or your relatives, or rich neighbors, in case they invite you back in return and you are repaid. But when you give a feast, call the poor, the crippled, the lame and the blind, and you will be blessed, because they have nothing to repay you with. You will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous." When one of those sitting at table with him heard this, he said to him: "Blessed is he who eats bread in the kingdom of God."

After this the Passover, the feast day of the Jews, was near. And it happened that as he was traveling to Jerusalem, he passed through the middle of Samaria and Galilee. And as he entered a certain village, ten men with leprosy came to meet him, and they stood at a distance. And they raised their voices, saying: "Jesus, master, have mercy on us."

When he saw them, he said: "Go and show yourselves to the priests." And it happened that as they went, they were cleansed. One of them, when he saw that he had been made clean, turned back, praising God with a loud voice. And he fell on his face at his feet, giving thanks; and he was a Samaritan.

Then Jesus answered and said: "Were not ten healed? And where are the nine? Was no one found to return and give glory to God except this man of a foreign people?" Then he said to him: "Get up now and go, for your faith has made you well."

Then he took the twelve aside again and said to them: "See, we are going up to Jerusalem, and everything that has been written through the prophets about the Son of Man will be fulfilled. He will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes, and they will hand him over to the Gentiles. He will be mocked and scourged and spat upon and crucified, and on the third day he will rise again."

Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee came to him with her sons, worshipping him, and asked something of him. He said to her: What do you want? Then she said to him: Say that these two sons of mine may sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your kingdom. Then Jesus answered and said to them: You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup that I am to drink, or be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized? Then they said to him: We can. Then he said to them: You will drink my cup, and you will be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized. But to sit at my right hand and at my left is not mine to give to you; it is for those for whom it has been prepared by my Father.

When the ten heard this, they were indignant with the two brothers. Jesus called them to him and said: You know that the rulers of the nations lord it over them, and those who are greater exercise authority over them. It shall not be so among you; rather, whoever wishes to be greater among you, let him be your servant, and whoever wishes to be first among you, let him be your slave. Just so, the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.

And then someone said to him: Lord, are those who are saved few? He said to them: Strive to enter through the narrow gate, because many, I tell you, sought to enter and could not. When the father of the household has gone in and shut the door, then you will begin to stand outside and knock, saying: Lord, open to us. And he will answer and say: I do not know you or where you are from. Then you will begin to say: We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets. And then he will say to you: I do not know you or where you are from; depart from me, all you workers of iniquity.

There will then be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when you see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets entering into the kingdom of God, and yourselves driven out. And they will come from the east and from the west, from the north and from the south, and will sit down in the kingdom of God. And then those who were first before will be last, and those who were last before will be first.

And he entered and was passing through Jericho. And behold, there was a man named Zacchaeus; he was the chief of the tax collectors, and he was rich. He sought to see Jesus, who he was, and could not because of the crowd, for he was small of stature. And running ahead, he climbed up into a mulberry tree (sycamore) so that he might see him, for he was going to pass by that way. And when he came to the place, Jesus looked up, saw him, and said to him: Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay at your house. And he came down in haste and received him with joy.

And when all saw it, they murmured, saying that he had turned in to a sinful man. Then Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord: "Behold, Lord, half of my goods I give to the needy; and if I have defrauded anyone in anything, I repay it fourfold." Then Jesus said to him: "Today salvation has come to this house, because he is a son of Abraham. The Son of Man came to seek and to save what was lost."

And as they went out from Jericho, a great crowd followed him. And behold, two blind men, one of whom was Bartimaeus son of Timaeus, sitting by the way, heard that Jesus of Nazareth was passing by there, and they cried out, saying: "Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!" The crowd rebuked them, telling them to be silent. But they cried out all the more, saying: "Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!"

And Jesus stood still and called them and said: "What do you want me to do for you?" Then they said to him: "Lord, that our eyes may be opened." Then Jesus had mercy on them and touched their eyes, and at once they saw, and they followed him, glorifying the Lord. And all the people, when they saw it, gave praise to God.

And when they drew near to Jerusalem and came to Bethphage, to the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two of his disciples, saying to them: "Go into the village that is opposite you, and at once you will find a she-ass tied up, and her foal tied with her, on which no man has ever sat. Untie it and lead it to me. And if anyone says anything to you, say to him: 'The Lord has need of its service,' and at once he will let them go."

The disciples went and did as Jesus had commanded them. As they were untying it, its owners said to them: "Why are you untying the foal?" They said: "Because the Lord has need of it." And they let them go, and they led the foal to Jesus, threw their garments over the foal, and set him on it.

This was done so that what had been spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, who said: "Say to the daughter of Zion: Behold, your king has come to you, meek, sitting on the foal of a tame she-ass." His disciples did not understand these things at first, but when Jesus was glorified, then they remembered that these things had been written about him, and that they had done these things to him.

As he went, many spread their garments on the way, and some cut branches from the trees and spread them on the way. And when he was already drawing near to the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole crowd of those coming down began, rejoicing, to praise God with a loud voice; the crowds that went before and those that followed after cried out, saying: "Hosanna (salvation and praise) to the Son of David! Blessed is the king who comes in the name of the Lord; peace to him in heaven and glory in the highest! Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David! Hosanna (salvation and praise) to him in the highest!"

On the next day a great crowd that had come to the feast, when they heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem, took branches of palm trees and went out to meet him and cried: Hail, blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, the king of Israel! And some of the Pharisees in the crowd said to him: Master, rebuke your disciples. Then he said to them: I tell you that if these keep silent, the stones will cry out.

And then he drew near, and seeing the city he wept over it, saying: If only you had understood, and indeed on this your day, the things that are for your peace! But now they are hidden from your eyes. For days will come upon you, and they will surround you and hem you in on every side, and they will dash you to the ground, and the children who are within you, and they will not leave one stone upon another in you, because you did not understand the time of your visitation.
When he then entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred, saying: Who is this? The crowds said: This is Jesus, the prophet from the city of Nazareth in Galilee.

And Jesus entered the temple of God, and when he had made a kind of whip out of cords, he drove out all who were selling and those who were buying in the temple, the sheep and the cattle, and the tables of the money-changers; he poured out the coins and overturned the seats of those who sold the doves,

and said to them: Take these things away from here, and do not make the house of my Father a house of trade. It is written: My house shall be called a house of prayer for all nations; but you have made it a den of thieves. And he would not allow anyone to carry a vessel through the temple. Then his disciples remembered that it is written: Zeal for your house has consumed me. And the blind and the lame came to him in the temple, and he healed them.

Then the chief priests and the scribes saw the signs that he did, and the boys crying out in the temple and saying: Hail to the son of David! They became indignant and said to him: Do you hear what these are saying? Jesus said to them: Have you never read that out of the mouth of children and infants at the breast you have brought praise to perfection? Then the Jews answered and said to him: What sign do you show us, seeing that you do these things?

Then Jesus answered and said to them: Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. Then the Jews said: This temple was forty-six years in building, and you will raise it up in three days? But he said that about the temple of his body.
