Then, looking on, he saw the rich people who were putting their gifts into the treasury. He also saw a certain poor widow putting in two bronze coins, that is, a quadrans. And he called his disciples and said to them: Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all of them. For all these put into the offerings to God out of their abundance; but she, out of what she lacked, put in all the living that she had.

Then he spoke this parable to some who trusted in themselves as if they were righteous and despised others: Two men went up into the temple to pray; one was a Pharisee and the other was a tax collector. The Pharisee, standing, prayed these things to himself: God, I give you thanks that I am not like other men, robbers, unjust, adulterers, or like this tax collector. I fast twice a week; I give tithes of all that I possess.

And the tax collector, standing far off, would not even lift his eyes to heaven, but struck his breast, saying: God, be merciful to me, a sinner. I say to you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other, because everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and he who humbles himself will be exalted.

And having left them, when it was already evening, he went out of the city to the place called Bethany, and stayed there. And the crowd, knowing that he had gone out of the city, followed him, and receiving them, he healed those who had need of healing.

There was a man of the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews. He came to him by night and said to him: Master, we know that you have come from God as a teacher; no one can do these signs that you do unless God is with him.

Then the Savior answered and said to him: Truly, truly I say to you, unless someone is born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God. Then Nicodemus said to him: How can a man be born when he is old? How can he enter again into his mother's womb and be born?

Then the Savior answered: Truly, truly I say to you, unless someone is born again of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God. What is born of the flesh is flesh, and what is born of the Spirit is spirit.

Do not wonder that I said to you: you must be born again. The Spirit blows where it wills, and you hear its voice, yet you do not know where it comes from or where it goes. So is everyone who is born of the Spirit.
Then Nicodemus answered and said to him: How can these things be?

Then the Savior answered and said to him: You are a teacher of Israel and you do not know this? Truly, truly I say to you, we speak what we know, and we testify to what we have seen, and you do not receive our testimony.

If I have told you earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you heavenly things? And no one ascends into heaven except him who descended from heaven, the Son of Man who is in heaven.
And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish but have eternal life.
God so loved this world that he gave his only Son, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish but have eternal life.
God did not send his Son into the world to judge the world, but so that the world might be saved through him.
Whoever believes in him is not judged; whoever does not believe is already judged, because he did not believe in the name of the only-begotten Son of God.

This is the judgment: the light came into the world, and people loved darkness more than light, for their works were evil. Everyone who does evil hates the light and does not come to the light, so that his works may not be reproved. Whoever does what is true comes to the light, so that his works may be made manifest, because they are done from God.
And each one went to his own house.
Jesus went to the Mount of Olives, and early in the morning he came again into the temple, and all the people came to him, and he sat down and taught them.
Then the scribes and Pharisees brought a woman caught in adultery and set her in the middle, among them.
And they said to him: Master, this woman has just now been caught in adultery.
In the law Moses commanded us to stone such women. What do you say about it?
They said this to test him, so that they might accuse him. Then Jesus bent down and wrote on the ground with his finger.
When they kept on questioning him, he straightened up and said to them: Let whoever among you is without sin be the first to throw a stone at her.

Then he bent down again and wrote on the ground. When they heard that, they went out one after another, beginning with the elders, and Jesus was left there alone, with the woman standing in the middle. Then Jesus straightened up and said to her: Woman, where are those who accused you? Has no one condemned you?
Then she said: No one, Lord. Then Jesus said: Neither do I condemn you. Go now, and do not choose to sin any more.

In the morning, as he was returning to the city, he was hungry. And he saw a fig tree near the road and came to it, and found nothing on it except leaves only, for it was not yet the season for figs. And he said to it: May no fruit ever be born from you again, for ever! Then at once the fig tree withered. When the disciples saw that, they marveled greatly and said: Look how quickly it has withered!

When evening came, they went out of the city. And when they passed by in the morning, they saw that the fig tree had withered from the roots. Then Peter remembered and said to him: Master, look, the fig tree that you cursed has withered.

Then Jesus answered and said to them: Have faith in God. Truly I tell you, if you have faith and do not doubt in your heart, you will not only do what was done to the one fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, 'Take yourself up and throw yourself into the sea,' it will be so.

Then the apostles said to him: Lord, increase our faith. Then Jesus said: Whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you receive it, and it will come to you. And when you stand to pray, forgive, if you hold anything against anyone, so that your Father who is in heaven may forgive you your sins.
Then he spoke to them in a likeness and parable, because one ought always to pray and not to give up. There was a certain judge in a certain city who did not fear God and had no regard for man.

There was also a certain widow in that city, and she came to him, saying: "Avenge me of my adversary." And for a long time he would not. Afterwards he said within himself: "Even though I neither fear God nor dread man, yet because this widow is troublesome to me, I will avenge her, lest perhaps by coming at the last she wear me out."

Then the Lord said: "Hear what the unrighteous judge said. Will not God then do justice for his chosen ones, who cry to him day and night, and will he be patient with them? I say to you that he will quickly do them justice. Yet when the Son of Man comes, do you think that he will find faith on the earth?"

When he then came into the temple, it came to pass, as he was teaching the people and preaching, that the chief priests and the elders of the people came to him, saying: "By what authority do you do these things?"

Then Jesus answered and said to them: "I will also ask you one thing; if you tell it to me, then I will tell you by what authority I do these things. Where was John's baptism from, from heaven or from men?" Then they reasoned among themselves, saying: "If we say 'from men,' then we fear the multitude, for all hold John to be a prophet."
Then they answered Jesus and said: "We do not know." Then he said to them: "Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things."

"What do you think? A certain man had two sons, and he went to the first and said to him: 'Son, go today and work in my vineyard.' He answered and said: 'I will not.' Afterwards, moved by repentance, he went there.
Then he went to the other and said the same to him. He answered and said: 'I am going, lord,' and he did not go.
Which of the two did the father's will?" Then they said: "The younger." Then Jesus said to them: "Truly I say to you, the sinful men and the harlots go before you into the kingdom of God.

John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him; the sinful men and the harlots believed him. And you, though you saw that, had no repentance afterwards, so that you might believe him.

Hear another parable: There was a man, a father of a household, who planted a vineyard, and put a fence around it, and dug a winepress in it, and built a tower, and entrusted it to the husbandmen, and went into a foreign land.

When the time of the fruits drew near, he sent his servants to the husbandmen, so that they might receive his fruit. Then the husbandmen seized his servants; one they flogged, another they killed, another they stoned.

Again he sent other servants, more than the first, and they did the same to them. Last of all he sent his son to them, saying: 'Perhaps they will respect my son.' The husbandmen, seeing the son, said among themselves: 'This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and we shall have his inheritance.' Then they seized him, threw him out of the vineyard, and killed him.

So when the lord of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those vinedressers? They said to him: He will destroy those wicked men wickedly, and will entrust the vineyard to other husbandmen, who will render him the fruit in their seasons.

Then the Saviour said to them: Have you never read in the Scriptures: The stone which the builders rejected, that has become the head of the corner? This was done by the Lord, and it is wonderful in our eyes. Therefore I say to you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and will be given to a people that produces its fruit. Whoever falls on that stone will be broken to pieces; on whomever it falls, it will crush him.

When the chief priests and the Pharisees heard his parables, they understood that he was speaking about them. And though they sought to seize him, they feared the crowd, because they held him to be a prophet.
Then the Saviour answered and spoke to them again in parables:
The kingdom of heaven is like a man, a king, who made a wedding feast for his son and invited many.
At the time of the feast he sent his servants to call those who had been invited to the wedding, and they would not come.
Then they all together began to make excuses. The first said to him: I have bought a farm, and I need to go out and see it; I ask you, consider me excused.
Then another said: I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to try them out; I ask you, consider me excused.
Then another also said: I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.
Again he sent other servants, saying: Tell those who are invited: Behold, I have prepared my dinner; my bulls and fatlings are slaughtered and everything is ready; come to the wedding.
But they paid no heed to it and went off, one to his farm, another to his trade. The others seized his servants, treated them shamefully, and killed them.
When the king heard this, he was enraged, and he sent his armies, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city.

Then he said to his servants: The wedding is ready, but those who were invited were not worthy. Go to the outlets of the roads, into the streets and into the villages and into the towns, and whomever you find, the poor and the maimed and the blind and the lame, invite them to the wedding.
Then the servant said: Lord, it has been done as you commanded, and there is still room.

Then the lord said to the servant: Go out into the roads and to the hedges and compel them to come in, so that my house may be filled. I tell you that none of those men who were invited shall taste my feast. Then his servants went out into the roads and gathered all whom they found, both bad and good, and the wedding hall was filled with guests. Then the king went in to see the guests, and he saw there a man who was not clothed in a wedding garment. And he said to him: Friend, how did you come in here without a wedding garment? Then the king said to the attendants: Bind his feet and hands and cast him into the outer darkness; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth. Many are invited, but few are chosen.

Then the Pharisees went off and took counsel together on how they might trap him in his words. And they sent their disciples to him with Herod's men, saying: "Master, we know that you are truthful and teach the way of God in truth, and you are not concerned about anyone, for you do not regard the person of men. Tell us what you think: is it lawful to pay tribute to the emperor or not?"
Perceiving their wickedness, the Savior said: "Why do you test me, you hypocrites? Show me the coin of the tribute." Then they brought him a penny.

Then the Savior said to them: "Whose is this image and the inscription on it?" They said to him: "The emperor's." Then he said to them: "Render to the emperor the things that are the emperor's, and to God the things that are God's." When they heard this they marvelled, and they left him and went away.

On that day Sadducees, who say that there is no resurrection, came to him and asked him, saying: "Master, Moses said that if anyone dies without having sons, his brother should take his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.

There were among us seven brothers. The first took a wife and died, and having no offspring he left his wife to his brother. Likewise the second died without a child, and the third took her, and so all seven, and they left no offspring. Last of all the woman died. In the resurrection, whose wife will she be of them? For they all had her."

Then the Savior said to them: "You are in error, knowing neither the Scriptures nor the power of God. The children of this world marry and are given in marriage; but those who are counted worthy of that world and of the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor take wives, nor can they die any more, but they are like God's angels in heaven and are children of God, since they are children of the resurrection.

But as to the dead rising: have you not read in the books of Moses, at the passage about the thorn-bush, what was spoken by God, how God said to him: 'I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob'? He is not the God of the dead but of the living, for all live to him. You are greatly in error."
When the crowds heard this, they marvelled at his teaching. Then some of the scribes answered and said: "Master, you have spoken well."

When the Pharisees saw that he had silenced the Sadducees, they gathered together. And then one of the scribes, a teacher of the law, came to test him, saying: "Master, which is the great commandment in the law?"

Then the Savior said to him: "The first of all the commandments is: Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God is one God; and you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength. This is the first and greatest commandment.
The second is like it: that you shall love your neighbor as yourself. On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets."

Then the scribe said to him: Well, master, you have said in truth that he is one and there is no other besides him. And that he should be loved with all the heart and with all the understanding and with all the soul and with all the strength, and that one should love one's neighbour as oneself, is more than all burnt offerings and sacrifices.
Then the Saviour, seeing that he answered wisely, said to him: You are not far from the kingdom of God. You have answered rightly: do this and you will live.
Then, wishing to justify himself, he said to the Saviour: Who is my neighbour?

Then the Saviour took this up and said: A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell among thieves, who robbed him, and after they had inflicted wounds on him they went away, leaving him half dead.
Then it happened that a certain priest went down by the same road, and when he saw him he passed by. The Levite did the same: when he was near the place and saw him, he passed by.

A certain man of another people, travelling, came near him, and seeing him he was moved with compassion. He came close and bound up his wounds, pouring oil and wine on them, and setting him on his own beast he brought him to an innkeeper's house and took care of him. The next day he brought out two pennies, gave them to the innkeeper and said: Take care of him, and whatever you spend beyond this, I will repay you when I come back.
Which of these three seems to you to have been neighbour to the man who fell among the thieves? Then he said: The one who showed mercy to him. Then the Saviour said to him: Go and do likewise.

And he was teaching daily in the temple. The chief priests and the scribes and the leaders of the people sought to destroy him, and did not find what they could do to him, for all the people were eager to hear him.
The Pharisees heard the crowd murmuring these things about him; then the chief priests and the Pharisees sent officers to seize him.
Then the Saviour said: Yet a little while I am with you, and then I go to him who sent me. You will seek me and not find me, and where I am, there you cannot come.

Then the Jews said among themselves: Where will this man go, that we shall not find him? Will he go to those dispersed among the Gentiles and teach the Gentiles? What is this saying that he said: You will seek me and not find me, and where I am, there you cannot come?

On the last, great day of the feast the Saviour stood and cried out, saying: If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink! Whoever believes in me, as the Scripture says, rivers of living water will flow from his belly.
He said this about the Spirit, which those who believed in him were to receive: the Spirit had not been given, because the Saviour was not yet glorified.

Then some of the crowd, when they heard his words, said: "This is truly a prophet." Others said: "This is the Christ." Some said: "Surely the Christ does not come out of Galilee? Indeed, the scripture says that the Christ comes from the seed of David and from the town of Bethlehem, where David was." So there was dissension in the crowd because of him.
Then the officers came to the chief priests and the Pharisees, and these said to them: "Why did you not bring him?" Then the officers answered: "Never did any man speak as this man does."

Then the Pharisees answered them: "Surely you have not been led astray as well? Has any one of the rulers or of the Pharisees believed in him? But this crowd, which does not know the law, is accursed."
Then Nicodemus, who had come to him by night and who was one of them, said to them: "Does our law judge a man without first hearing from him and learning what he does?"
Then they answered and said to him: "Surely you are not a Galilean too? Search and see that no prophet arises out of Galilee."
When the Pharisees were gathered together, the Savior asked them, saying: "What do you think of the Christ? Whose son is he?" Then they said to him: "David's."

Then he said to them: "How is it that David himself, in the book, calls him Lord, saying: 'The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet'? If David truly calls him Lord in the spirit, how is he his son?"
And no one could answer him a word, nor did anyone dare from that day on to ask him anything more.
Again the Savior spoke to them, saying: "I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me does not walk in darkness, but has the light of life."
Then the Pharisees said to him: "You bear witness about yourself; your witness is not true."

Then the Savior answered and said to them: "Even if I bear witness about myself, my witness is true, because I know where I came from and where I am going; but you do not know where I come from or where I am going.
You judge according to the flesh; I judge no one. If I do judge, then my judgment is true, because I am not alone; rather it is I and he who sent me, the Father
. And in your law it is written: the witness of two men is true. I am the one who bears witness about myself, and the one who sent me, the Father, bears witness about me

. Then they said to him: "Where is your father?" Then the Savior answered: "You know neither me nor my Father; if you knew me, perhaps you would also know my Father. I am going away, and you will seek me, and you will die in your sin. Where I am going, there you cannot come

. Then the Jews said: "Surely he will not kill himself, since he says: 'Where I am going, you cannot come'?" Then he said to them: "You are from below; I am from above. You are of this world; I am not of this world. I tell you that you will die in your sins: if you do not believe that I am, then you will die in your sin

Then they said to him: "Who are you?" Then the Savior said to them: "The beginning, which I am also speaking to you. I have many things to say and to judge concerning you. But he who sent me is true, and the things I have heard from him, these I speak in the world."

And they did not understand that he was speaking to them of the Father as God. Then the Savior said to them: "When you lift up the Son of Man, then you will understand that I am he, and that I do nothing of myself, but as the Father taught me, so I speak these things. And he who sent me is with me: he does not leave me alone, because I always do the things that are pleasing to him." As he was saying these things, many believed in him. Then the Savior said to the Jews who believed him: "If you remain in my word, then you are truly my disciples, and then you will know the truth, and the truth [will] set you free."
Then they answered him: "We are the seed of Abraham and have never at any time been servants to anyone. How can you say: 'You will be free'?"
Then the Savior answered them: "Truly, truly I say to you, everyone who commits sin is the servant of sin. The servant does not remain in the house forever; the son remains forever."

"If the Son sets you free, then you will be truly free. I know that you are Abraham's children; yet you seek to kill me, because my word does not take hold in you. What I have seen with my Father, that I speak; and you do what you have seen with your father."

Then they answered and said to him: "Our father is Abraham." Then the Savior said to them: "If you are Abraham's children, then do the works of Abraham. But now you seek to kill me, a man who has told you the truth, which I heard from God. Abraham did not do this."
"You do the works of your father." Then they said to him: "We were not born of fornication; we have one father, God."

Then the Savior said to them: "If God were your father, then you would love me. I came forth from God and have come; I did not come of myself, but he sent me. Why do you not understand my speech? Because you cannot hear my word."

"You are of your father the devil, and you want to do your father's desires. He was a murderer from the beginning and did not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks a lie, he speaks from his own, for he is a liar and its father."

"But because I speak the truth, you do not believe me. Which of you convicts me of sin? If I speak the truth, why do you not believe me? Whoever is of God hears the word of God; you do not hear it for this reason, because you are not of God."
Then the Jews answered and said to him: "Are we not right to say that you are a Samaritan and have a devil?"

The Savior answered: "I do not have a devil, but I honor my Father, and you dishonor me. I do not seek my own glory; there is one who seeks it and judges. Truly, truly I say to you, whoever keeps my word will never see death."

. Then the Jews said: Now we know that you have a devil. Abraham is dead, and the prophets, and you say: Whoever keeps my word will never taste death. Are you greater than our father Abraham, who is dead? And the prophets are dead too. Whom do you make yourself

? Then the Saviour answered: If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing. It is my Father who glorifies me, of whom you say that he is your God, and you have not known him. But I know him, and if I said that I do not know him, I would be a liar like you. But I know him and keep his word. Abraham your father rejoiced that he would see my day, and he saw it and rejoiced. Then the Jews said to him: You are not yet fifty years old, and you have seen Abraham? Then the Saviour said to them: Truly, truly I say to you, before Abraham was, I am
. Then they took up stones to throw at him. But he hid himself and went out of the temple.
As he passed by, he saw a man who had been blind from birth. And his disciples asked him: Master, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?
Then the Saviour answered: Neither this man sinned nor his parents, but this happened so that the works of God might be shown in him.
I must work the works of him who sent me while it is day. Night is coming, when no one can work. As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.

When he had said this, he spat on the ground and made clay from the spittle, and spread the clay over his eyes, and said to him: Go and wash yourself in the water of Siloam, which means 'sent'. So he went and washed himself, and came back seeing.

Then the neighbours, and those who had seen him before, when he was a beggar, said: Is this not the man who used to sit and beg? Some said: It is he. Others said: No, but he is like him. But he himself said: I am the one.

Then they said to him: How were your eyes opened? He answered: The man who is called the Saviour made clay and spread it on my eyes and said to me: Go to the water of Siloam and wash yourself. And I went and washed, and I could see.
Then they said to him: Where is he? He said: I do not know. Then they brought the man who had been blind to the Pharisees. It was the Sabbath when the Saviour made the clay and opened his eyes.
The Pharisees also asked him again how he had received his sight. He said to them: He put clay on my eyes, and I washed, and I could see.
Some of the Pharisees said: This man is not from God, because he does not keep the Sabbath. Others said: How can a sinful man do such signs? And there was division among them.
Then they said to the blind man again: What do you say about the man who opened your eyes? He said: That he is a prophet.

The Jews did not believe that he had been blind and had received his sight until they called his parents, who had seen it, and questioned them, saying: Is this your son, who you say was born blind? How then does he see now?

Then his parents answered them and said: "We know that this is our son and that he was born blind. But how he now sees, we do not know, or who opened his eyes, we do not know. Ask him: he is of age; let him speak for himself."

His parents said this because they feared the Jews, for the Jews had already agreed among themselves that if anyone confessed him to be Christ, he would be put out of the synagogue. That is why his parents said: "He is of age; ask him himself."
So they called again the man who had been blind and said to him: "Give glory to God. We know that this man is a sinner."
Then he said: "Whether he is a sinner I do not know. One thing I know: I was blind, and now I see." Then they said to him: "What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?"
Then he answered them: "I have told you already, and you heard. Why do you want to hear it again? Do you want to become his disciples?"
Then they cursed him and said: "You be his disciple; we are disciples of Moses. We know that God spoke to Moses, but as for this man, we do not know where he comes from."

Then the man answered and said to them: "Here is a wonder: you do not know where he comes from, and yet he opened my eyes! We know truly that God does not hear sinners; but if anyone is a worshipper of God and does his will, God hears him."
"Since the world began it has never been heard that anyone opened the eyes of a man born blind. If this man were not from God, he could not do anything of the kind."
Then they answered and said to him: "You were born entirely in sins, and you are teaching us?" And they threw him out.
The Savior heard that they had thrown him out. When he found him, he said to him: "Do you believe in the Son of God?" Then he answered and said: "Who is he, Lord, that I may believe in him?"
Then the Savior said to him: "You have seen him, and the one who is speaking with you is he." Then he said to him: "I believe, Lord," and falling down he worshipped him.
Then the Savior said to him: "I came into this world for judgment, so that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind."
And some of the Pharisees who were with him heard this and said to him: "Are we then blind?"
Then the Savior said to them: "If you were blind, you would have no sin. But now you say, 'We see,' so your sin remains."

"Truly, truly I say to you: whoever does not go in through the door into the sheepfold but climbs in some other way is a thief and a robber. Whoever goes in through the door is the shepherd of the sheep. The doorkeeper opens to him, and the sheep hear his voice, and he calls his own sheep by name and leads them out."

"And when he has sent out his own sheep, he goes ahead of them, and the sheep follow him because they know his voice. They do not follow a stranger but flee from him, because they do not know the voice of strangers."
The Savior told them this parable, but they did not understand what he was saying to them.
Then the Savior said to them again: "Truly, truly I say to you, I am the door of the sheep. All who came before me are thieves and robbers, and the sheep did not listen to them."

I am the door. If anyone enters through me, he will be saved, and he will go in and go out and find pasture. The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy. I came so that they may have life and have it in abundance.

I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for his sheep. But the hired man, who is not the shepherd and does not own the sheep, sees the wolf coming, leaves the sheep and runs away, and the wolf tears and scatters the sheep. The hired man runs away because he is a hired man and does not care about the sheep.
I am the good shepherd, and I know my own, and my own know me. As my Father knows me, so I know my Father, and I lay down my life for my sheep.
And I have other sheep that are not of this fold. I must bring them too, and they will hear my voice, and then there will be one fold and one shepherd.

This is why my Father loves me: because I lay down my life and take it up again. No one takes it from me, but I lay it down of my own accord. I have power to lay it down and power to take it up again. I received this command from my Father.
Again there was division among the Jews because of these words.
Then many of them said: "He has a devil and is raving. Why do you listen to him?" Others said: "These are not the words of a man who has a devil. Can a devil open the eyes of the blind?"
Then the Feast of Dedication was held in Jerusalem, and it was winter. And the Savior was walking in the temple, in Solomon's porch.
The Jews surrounded him and said to him: "How long will you take away our souls? If you are the Christ, tell us plainly."
Then the Savior answered them: "I tell you, and you do not believe. The works that I do in my Father's name bear witness about me. But you do not believe, because you are not of my sheep.
My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me. I give them eternal life, and they will never perish, and no one will take them from my hand.
What my Father has given me is greater than all, and no one can snatch it from my Father's hand. I and the Father are one."
Then the Jews picked up stones to stone him. Then the Savior answered them: "I have shown you many good works from my Father. For which of those works are you stoning me?"
The Jews answered him: "We are not stoning you for a good work, but for blasphemy, and because you, though you are a man, make yourself God."

Then the Savior answered them: "Is it not written in your law, 'I said, you are gods'? If he called them gods to whom the word of God came, and scripture cannot be broken, do you say to him whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, 'You are blaspheming,' because I said, 'I am the Son of God'?

If I do not do my Father's works, do not believe me. But if I do them, even if you will not believe me, believe the works, so that you may understand and believe that the Father is in me and I am in the Father."
They tried to seize him, and he slipped out of their hands. And he went back across the Jordan to the place where John had first been baptizing, and stayed there.
And many came to him and said: "John did no sign, but everything John said about this man was true." And many believed in him.

There was a certain sick man, Lazarus of Bethany, of the town of Mary and her sister Martha. Mary was the one who anointed the Lord with ointment and wiped his feet with her hair; it was her brother Lazarus who had fallen sick.

Then his sisters sent to him and said: "Lord, the one you love is sick." Hearing that, the Savior said to them: "This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it."
The Savior loved Martha and her sister Mary and Lazarus. So when he heard that he was sick, he stayed two days in the same place.
After that he said to his disciples: "Let us go into Judea again." Then the disciples said to him: "Master, the Jews were just now trying to stone you, and are you going there again?"

Then the Savior answered: "Are there not twelve hours in the day? If anyone walks in the day, he does not stumble, because he sees the light of this world. If he walks in the night, he stumbles, because the light is not in him."

He said these things, and after that he said to them: "Lazarus our friend is sleeping, but I am going so that I may wake him from sleep." Then his disciples said to him: "Lord, if he is sleeping, then he will be well."

The Savior had spoken of his death, but they thought he was speaking of the rest of sleep. Then the Savior told them plainly: "Lazarus is dead. And for your sake I am glad that I was not there, so that you may believe. But let us go to him!"
Then Thomas, who is called Didymus, said to his fellow disciples: "Let us go too, so that we may die with him."
Then the Savior came and found that he had already been in the tomb four days. Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia away.
Many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary to comfort them about their brother.
Now when Martha heard that the Savior was coming, she ran to meet him; Mary stayed sitting in the house.
Then Martha said to the Savior: "Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died. But even now I know that whatever you ask of God, he will give you."
Then the Savior said to her: "Your brother will rise again."
Then Martha said to him: "I know that he will rise again in the resurrection on the last day."
Then the Savior said to her: "I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, even if he dies, will live; and everyone who lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?"
Then she said to him: "Yes, Lord, I have believed that you are the Christ, the Son of God, who has come into the world."
When she had said this, she went and called her sister Mary, saying quietly: "The Master is here and is asking for you." When she heard this, she got up quickly and came to him.
The Savior had not yet come into the village, but was still at the place where Martha had met him.
The Jews who were with her in the house and were comforting her saw Mary get up quickly and go out. They followed her, saying: "Now she is going to the tomb to weep there."
When Mary came to where the Saviour was and saw him, she fell at his feet and said to him: "Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died."

When the Saviour saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her weeping too, he groaned in his spirit and was troubled, and he said: "Where have you laid him?" They said to him: "Lord, come and see!" And the Saviour wept.
Then the Jews said: "See how he loved him!" But some of them said: "Could not this man, who opened the eyes of the blind man, have made it so that this man would not die?"
The Saviour, again groaning within himself, came to the tomb. It was a cave, and a stone was set over it.

The Saviour said: "Take away the stone!" Then the dead man's sister said to him: "Lord, he already stinks, for he has been there four days." Then the Saviour said to her: "Did I not tell you that if you believe, you will see the glory of God?"

Then they took away the stone. The Saviour raised his eyes and said: "Father, I give you thanks, for you have heard me. I knew that you always hear me, but I said this for the sake of the people standing around, so that they may believe that you sent me."

When he had said this, he cried out with a loud voice: "Lazarus, come out!" And at once the man who had been dead came out, his hands and feet bound with cords and his face bound with a sweat-cloth. Then the Saviour said to them: "Untie him and let him go."
Many of the Jews who had come to Mary and had seen what he did believed in him. But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what the Saviour had done.

The chief priests and the Pharisees called an assembly and said: "What shall we do? For this man is doing many signs. If we let him go on like this, everyone will believe in him, and the Romans will come and take away our place and our nation."

One of them, Caiaphas, who was high priest that year, said to them: "You know nothing at all. You do not consider that it is better for us that one man should die for the people than that the whole nation should perish."

He did not say this of his own accord. Because he was high priest that year, he prophesied that the Saviour was going to die for the nation. And not only for the nation, but also to gather into one the children of God who were scattered.
From that day on they planned to kill him.
So the Saviour no longer went about openly among the Jews. Instead he went to the region near the wilderness, to the town called Ephraim, and he stayed there with his disciples.
The Jewish Passover was near, and many people went up from the countryside to Jerusalem before the Passover to purify themselves.

Then they were looking for Jesus, and as they stood in the temple they said among themselves: "What do you think? Is he not coming to the feast day?" The chief priests and the Pharisees had given an order that if anyone found out where he was, he should report it, so that they could seize him.

Then it happened that, when the days of his being taken up were fulfilled, he set his face firmly to go to Jerusalem and sent messengers ahead of him. They went on their way and entered a town of the Samaritans to make things ready for him.
And they did not receive him, because his face was set toward Jerusalem.

When his disciples James and John saw this, they said: "Lord, do you want us to command fire to come down from heaven and burn them up?" Then he turned to them and rebuked them. And they went to another town.
Six days before Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, where Lazarus had been dead, whom Jesus had raised.

While he was in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, a great crowd of the Jews learned that he was there. They came not only because of Jesus but also to see Lazarus, whom he had raised from death.
The Pharisees said among themselves: "Do you see that we are getting nowhere? Look, now the whole world is going after him."
The chief priests planned to kill Lazarus as well, because on his account many of the Jews were leaving them and believing in Jesus.
There they made a supper for him. Martha served, and Lazarus was one of those who sat at table with him.

Mary had a jar of costly ointment made of nard. She broke it and poured it over his head as he reclined at table. She anointed his feet and wiped them with her hair, and the house was filled with the scent of the ointment.
Then one of his disciples, Judas Iscariot, who was going to betray him, said: "Why was this ointment not sold for three hundred pennies and the money given to the poor?"
He said this not because he cared about the poor, but because he was a thief. He kept the money bag and carried off what was put into it.
Some of them were indignant among themselves and said: "Why has this ointment been wasted?"

Jesus knew this and said to them: "Why are you troubling the woman? She has done a good work for me. You always have the poor with you, and whenever you want you can do good to them. But you do not always have me."
"By pouring this ointment on my body, she has prepared me for burial. Truly I tell you, wherever this gospel is preached in the whole world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her."

When the Pharisee who had invited him saw this, he said to himself: "If this man were a prophet, he would surely know who this woman touching him is and what kind of woman she is, because she is a sinner."
Jesus answered and said to him: "Simon, I have something to say to you." He said: "Master, say it."
"A certain moneylender had two debtors. One owed five hundred pennies, the other owed fifty. When they had nothing to pay him back with, he forgave them both. Which of them loved him more?"
Then Simon answered and said: I suppose that it is the one to whom he forgave more. Then he said to him: You have judged rightly.
And turning to the woman, he said: Simon, do you see this woman? I came into your house: you gave no water for my feet, but this woman wet them with her tears and wiped them with her hair.
You gave me no kiss, but this woman, from the time she came in, has not stopped kissing my feet. You did not anoint my head with oil, but this woman anointed my feet with ointment.
Therefore I say to you: her many sins are forgiven her, because she loved much. The one to whom less is forgiven loves less. Then he said to her: Your sins are forgiven you.
Then those who sat there with him began to say among themselves: Who is this who even forgives sins? Then he said to the woman: Your faith has made you whole; go in peace.
When he had said these things, he went on, going up to Jerusalem.

There were some Gentiles among those who went up to worship on the feast day. They came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee, and asked him, saying: Lord, we wish to see Jesus. Then Philip came and told Andrew, and Andrew and Philip told Jesus.
Jesus answered them, saying: The hour is coming in which the Son of Man will be glorified.

Truly, truly I say to you: unless the grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone by itself; if it dies, it brings much fruit. Whoever loves his life will lose it; whoever hates his life in this world will keep it for eternal life.
If anyone serves me, let him follow me: where I am, there my servant will be. If anyone serves me, my Father will honor him.
Now my soul is troubled. And what shall I say? Father, save me from this hour! But it was for this that I came to this hour.
Father, glorify your name! A voice came from heaven: I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again.
The crowd that stood there and heard it said that it had thundered; others said: An angel spoke to him. Then Jesus answered and said: This voice did not come for my sake, but for yours.

Now is the judgment of this world; now the ruler of this world will be cast out. And I, if I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all things to myself. He said this to signify by what death he was going to die.
Then the crowd answered him: We have heard from the law that the Christ remains forever, so how can you say: The Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?

Then Jesus said: The light is among you for only a little while longer. Walk while you have the light, so that darkness does not overtake you: whoever walks in darkness does not know where he is going. While you have the light, believe in the light, so that you may be children of light.

When he was asked by the Pharisees when the kingdom of God would come, he answered them and said: The kingdom of God does not come with observation, nor will people say: Look, here it is, or there, for the kingdom of God is within you.
By day he was teaching in the temple, and at night he stayed on the mountain that is called the Mount of Olives; and all the people came to him early in the morning in the temple to hear him.

Then the Savior spoke to the crowds and to his disciples, and said: "The scribes and Pharisees have sat down on the seat of Moses. Keep and do everything they tell you, but do not choose to act as they act: they say, and do not do.
They bind heavy and unbearable burdens and lay them on people's shoulders, but they will not touch them with their own fingers.
They do all their works so that people will see them. They broaden their phylacteries and make large the fringes [?] on their garments.
They love the first places at feasts, the first seats in the synagogues, greetings in the street, and being called master by people."
All the people listened to him gladly.
"Do not choose to be called master: you have one master, and you are all brothers.
And do not call anyone on earth your father: you have one father, the one in heaven.
Nor are you to be called masters, because you have one master, Christ.
Whoever is greater among you is your servant. Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
Woe to you Pharisees, because you love the first seats in the assemblies and greetings in the street.

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, teachers of the law, hypocrites, because you have taken away the key of knowledge and shut the kingdom of heaven in people's faces. You do not go in yourselves, and you do not let those who are going in enter.
Woe to you, Pharisees, hypocrites, who devour the houses of widows while pretending to make long prayers: you will receive the greater condemnation.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, who travel around sea and land to make a single proselyte, and when he has become one, you make him a son of hell twice as much as yourselves.

Woe to you, blind guides, who say: 'If anyone swears by the temple, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gold of the temple is bound by his oath.' Fools and blind! Which is greater, the gold, or the temple that makes the gold holy?
And: 'If anyone swears by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gift that is on it is bound by his oath.' Blind ones! Which is greater, the gift, or the altar that makes the gift holy?

Whoever swears by the altar swears by it and by everything on it. Whoever swears by the temple swears by it and by the one who dwells in it. Whoever swears by heaven swears by God's throne and by the one who sits on it.

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, who pay tithes of mint and dill and cumin and rue and every herb, and have neglected the weightier matters of the law: justice and mercy and faith and the love of God.
You ought to have done these things without neglecting the others. Blind guides, straining out a gnat and swallowing a camel!
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but inside they are full of plunder and uncleanness.
You blind Pharisee, first clean the inside of the cup and the dish, so that the outside may be clean too.
Woe to you, because you are like hidden graves, and people walking over them do not know it.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you are like whitewashed tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful to men but inside are full of the bones of the dead and of every kind of filth.
So you, too, outwardly appear righteous to men, but inside you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.
Then one of those learned in the law answered and said to him: "Master, by saying this you [?] insult us as well."
Then he said: "Woe also to you who are learned in the law, because you load men with burdens that they cannot bear, and you yourselves do not touch the burden with one of your fingers."

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you build the tombs of the prophets and adorn the tombs of the righteous, and say: "If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have been their partners in shedding the blood of the prophets."
You are witnesses against yourselves that you are the children of those who killed the prophets. And you fill up the measure of your fathers.
Brood of vipers, how will you escape the judgment of hell?

Therefore the divine Wisdom said: "I send to them prophets and apostles and wise men and scribes. Some of them you will kill and crucify, and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues and persecute from city to city, so that upon you may come all the righteous blood that has been shed on the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the temple and the altar."
Truly I say to you, all these things will come upon this generation.

Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those who are sent to you! How often I wanted to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you would not. Behold, now your house will be left to you desolate.
I say to you: you will not see me from now on until you say: "Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!"

Yet even so, many of the chief men believed in him, but because of the Pharisees they did not confess it, so that they would not be cast out of the synagogue. They loved the glory of men more than the glory of God.
Jesus cried out and said: "He who believes in me does not believe in me, but in him who sent me. He who sees me sees him who sent me.
I have come as a light into the world, so that everyone who believes in me does not remain in darkness.
But if anyone hears my words and does not keep them, I do not judge him. I did not come to judge the world, but to save the world.
He who rejects me and does not receive my words has one who judges him: the word that I have spoken will judge him on the last day.

For I do not speak of myself; rather, the Father who sent me gave me a commandment about what I should say and what I should speak, and I know that his commandment is eternal life. What I speak, I speak just as the Father told me."
Jesus spoke these things to them, and he went away and hid himself from them.

Though he had done so many signs before them, they did not believe in him, so that the word of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, which he spoke: Lord, who has believed what we have heard, and to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed? Isaiah said these things when he saw his glory and spoke of him.
And as the Saviour went out of the temple, his disciples came to him to show him the buildings of the temple, saying: Master, look at what stones and what buildings these are!
Then the Saviour answered and said: Do you see all these great buildings? Truly I say to you, days will come in which not one stone will be left here upon another that is not thrown down.

And as he sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, his disciples came to him privately and asked him, saying: Master, tell us, when will these things happen? What is the sign of your coming, when all these things begin to be brought to an end?
And he said to the disciples: Days will come when you will long to see one day of the Son of Man, and you will not see it.
See that no one leads you astray: many will come in my name, saying: I am the Christ, and they will lead many astray.
When you hear of battles, and rumours of battles, and conflicts, do not be troubled: it must happen this way, but the end is not yet.

Nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom, and then there will be diseases and famines and earthquakes in various places, and terrors from heaven and great signs. All these are the beginning of sorrows.
Then they will hand you over to tribulation and kill you, and you will be hated by all nations for my name's sake.
And not a hair of your head will perish, and by your patience you will possess your souls.
Settle it in your hearts not to prepare beforehand how you will answer: I will give you a mouth and wisdom which none of your adversaries will be able to withstand or contradict.

Then many will be caused to stumble and will betray one another, and they will hate one another. And many false prophets will arise and lead many astray. And because wickedness will abound, the love of many will grow cold; but whoever endures to the end will be saved.
And this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in all the world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come.

When you see the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place (let the one who reads understand!), when you see Jerusalem surrounded by an army, then you will know that its desolation is near.

Then those who are in Judea should flee to the mountains, and those who are in the midst of it should leave it, and those who are out in the country should not go into it. For these are days of vengeance, so that all the things that are written may be fulfilled.

Woe to those who are pregnant and those who are nursing in those days! For truly there will be great distress over the earth and wrath upon this people, and they will fall by the edge of the sword and be led captive into all nations, and Jerusalem will be trodden down by the nations until the times of the nations are fulfilled.
Pray truly that your flight may not be in winter or on the Sabbath. For then there will be great tribulation, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, nor ever will be again.

And there will be signs in the sun and in the moon and in the stars, and on earth distress of the nations because of the roaring of the sea and of the flowing waters, with men withering away from fear and from expectation of the things that will come upon the whole world.
And unless those days had been shortened, no flesh would be saved; but for the sake of the chosen those days will be shortened.

Then if anyone says, 'Look, here is Christ,' or 'there,' do not believe it. False Christs and false prophets will arise and will give great signs and wonders, so that even the chosen would be led into error, if that were possible. Look, I have told you beforehand.

If they say to you, 'Look, he is in the desert,' do not go out; 'Look, he is in the inner rooms [?],' do not believe it. For as the lightning goes out from the east and shows itself even to the west, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.

Immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light, and the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken. And then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with great power and majesty. Then he will send his angels with trumpets and a great voice, and they will gather his chosen from the four winds, from the heights of the heavens to their ends.
When these things begin to happen, look up and lift up your heads, because your redemption is drawing near.
Learn a parable from the fig tree. When its branch has become tender and its leaves have sprung forth, and all the trees, when they now bring forth their fruit, you know that summer is near.
So you also, when you see all these things happen, know that he is near, at the doors.
Truly I say to you, this generation will not pass away before all these things happen. Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.

Take heed to yourselves, so that your hearts are not weighed down with overeating and drunkenness and the cares of this life, and that day comes upon you suddenly; for like a snare it will come upon all who dwell on the face of the whole earth.
Watch, therefore, at all times, praying that you may be counted worthy to escape all these things that are to come, and to stand before the Son of Man.
You do not know when the time will be: of that day and hour no one knows, neither the Son of Man nor the angels in heaven, but the Father alone.

As it was in the days of Noah, so is the coming of the Son of Man. In the days before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, right up to the day when Noah went into the ark. They did not understand until the flood came and took them all away. So is the coming of the Son of Man.

It was the same in the days of Lot: they ate and drank, bought and sold, planted and built. But on the day when Lot went out of Sodom, it rained fire and brimstone from heaven and destroyed them all. It will be like this on the day when the Son of Man is revealed.
On that day, whoever is on the roof must not come down to take anything from his house, and whoever is in the field must not turn back to take his clothing. Remember Lot's wife.

Then two will be in the field: one is taken and the other is left. Two women will be grinding at one mill: one is taken and the other will be left. Two will be in one bed: one is taken and the other is left.
They answered and said to him, "Where, Lord?" He said to them, "Wherever the body is, there the eagles will gather."
It is like a man who went on a journey to a foreign land. He left his house, gave his servants authority over all their work, and ordered the doorkeeper to keep watch.
So keep watch, for you do not know when the lord is coming: in the evening, or at midnight, or at cockcrow, or in the morning. Otherwise he may come suddenly and find you sleeping.

Know this: if the father of the household knew at what hour the thief would come, he would certainly keep watch and would not let his house be broken into. So you too must be ready, because the Son of Man is coming at an hour that you do not know.
Peter said to him, "Lord, are you telling this parable to us, or to everyone?" "What I say to you, I say to everyone: keep watch!"
The Lord said, "Who, then, do you think is the faithful servant and wise steward whom the lord sets over his household, to give them their food at the proper time?"
Blessed is that servant whom his lord finds doing this when he comes. Truly I tell you, he will set him over all his possessions.

But suppose the wicked servant says in his heart, "My lord is delaying his coming," and then begins to beat his fellow servants and to eat and drink with drunkards. The lord of that servant will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he does not know. He will cut him to pieces and give him his place with the hypocrites and the unfaithful. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
Then the kingdom of heaven will be like ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom and the bride.
Five of them were foolish and five were wise. The five foolish ones took their lamps but took no oil with them. The wise ones, however, took oil in their vessels along with their lamps.
While the bridegroom was delayed, they all grew drowsy and fell asleep. At midnight a cry went up: "Look, the bridegroom is coming! Go out to meet him!"
Then all the virgins got up and trimmed their lamps.

Then the foolish said to the wise: "Give us some of your oil, because our lamps have gone out." Then the wise answered, saying: "No, lest perhaps there not be enough for us and for you. Go rather to those who sell, and buy for yourselves!"
While they went to buy, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with him to the wedding, and the door was shut.
At last the other maidens came, saying: "Lord, lord, open to us!" Then he answered and said: "Truly I say to you, I do not know you."
Watch, therefore, for you know neither the day nor the hour.

It is like a man going on a journey who called his servants and handed over to them his goods. To one he gave five talents, to another two, to another one, to each according to his own ability, and he set out at once.

Then the one who had received the five talents went and worked with them and gained another five. Likewise the one who had received two talents gained another two. The one who had received the one went and dug in the earth and hid his lord's money.
After a long time the lord of those servants came and settled accounts with them.

And the one who had received five talents came forward and brought another five talents, saying: "Lord, you handed over five talents to me; see, I have gained another five besides." Then his lord said to him: "Well done, good and faithful servant. Because you were faithful over a few things, I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord."

The one who had received two talents came forward and said: "Lord, you handed over two talents to me; see, I have gained another two." Then his lord said to him: "Well done, good and faithful servant. Because you were faithful over a few things, I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord."

Then the one who had received the one talent came forward and said: "Lord, I know that you are a hard man: you reap where you did not sow and gather where you did not scatter. And being afraid, I went and hid your talent in the earth. See, here you have what is yours."

Then his lord answered and said to him: "Wicked and lazy servant! Since you knew that I reap where I did not sow and gather where I did not scatter, you ought to have entrusted my money to the money-changers, and on my coming I would have received what is mine with interest. Take the one talent from him and give it to the one who has ten talents."

For to everyone who has, more will be given, and he will have abundance; but from the one who does not have, even what he seems to have will be taken away from him. And as for the useless servant, cast him out into the outer darkness: there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
Let your loins be girded and your lamps burning, and be like men waiting for their lord, for when he returns from the wedding, so that when he comes and knocks they may open to him at once.
Blessed are those servants whom the lord, when he comes, finds watching. Truly I say to you, he will gird himself and have them sit down, and he will go about and serve them.
And if he comes in the second watch, or if he comes in the third watch, and finds them so, blessed are those servants.
Then he said: A certain noble man went into a far country to receive a kingdom for himself and to return again.
Then, having called his ten servants, he gave them ten minas and said to them: Trade until I come.
His citizens hated him, and sent an embassy after him, saying: We do not want this man to reign over us.

And it came to pass, when he returned having received the kingdom, that he commanded that his servants to whom he had given the money be called, so that he might know how much each of them had gained by trading.
Then the first came, saying: Lord, your mina has gained ten minas. He said to him: Well done, you good servant; because you were faithful in a little, you shall have authority over ten cities.
And another came, saying: Lord, your mina has made five minas. To him he said: You too, be over five cities.
And another came, saying: Lord, behold your mina, which I have kept laid away in a napkin. I was afraid, because you are a harsh man: you take what you did not lay down and reap what you did not sow.

Then he said to him: Out of your own mouth I judge you, you wicked servant. Since I am a harsh man, taking what I did not lay down and reaping what I did not sow, why then did you not give my money to the table [the bankers], so that I, on coming, might have demanded it back with interest [?]?
And to those standing by he said: Take the mina from him and give it to the one who has ten minas.
And they said to him: Lord, he has ten minas.

I say to you that to everyone who has, it will be given; but from the one who does not have, what he has will be taken away from him. But as for those enemies of mine, the people who did not want me to reign over them, lead them here and slay them before me.
When the Son of Man comes in his majesty, and all the angels with him, then he will sit upon the throne of his majesty.

And all nations will be gathered before him, and then he will separate them from one another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats, and he will set the sheep at his right hand and the goats at his left.

Then the king will say to those who are at his right hand: Come, you blessed of my Father, and possess the kingdom prepared for you from the beginning of the world. I was hungry and you gave me food to eat; I was thirsty and you gave me drink; I was a stranger and you took me in; naked, and you clothed me; sick, and you visited me; I was in prison and you came to me.

Then the righteous answered him and said: Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you drink? When did we see you a stranger and take you in, or naked and clothe you? Or when did we see you sick or in prison and come to you?
And the king, answering, will say to them: Truly I say to you, inasmuch as you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me.

Then he will say to those who are on his left: Depart from me, you accursed, into the eternal fire that is prepared for the devil and his angels. I was hungry and you did not give me food; I was thirsty and you did not give me drink; I was a stranger and you did not take me in; naked, and you did not clothe me; sick and in prison, and you did not visit me.
Then they will answer and say: Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and did not serve you?
Then he will answer them, saying: Truly I say to you, as long as you did not do it for one of these least ones, you did not do it for me either.
And these will go into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.
And it came to pass, when the Savior had finished all these words, that he said to his disciples:
You know that after two days it will be the Passover, and the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified.
Then the chief priests and the elders of the people were gathered in the court of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas.
And they took counsel to seize the Savior by deceit and kill him. Then they said: Not on the feast day, lest perhaps there be an uproar among the people.
Then one of the twelve, who is called Judas Iscariot, went and spoke to the chief priests and to the officials, and said to them: What will you give me? And I will hand him over to you.
When they heard this they were glad of it, and they promised him thirty coins; and from then on he sought an opportunity to hand him over to them away from the crowd.
Before the feast day of the Passover, the Savior knew that the hour had come for him to depart from this world to the Father. Having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them to the end.

Then he rose from the supper and laid aside his garments; and when he had taken a towel, he girded himself with it. Then he poured water into a basin and began to wash his disciples' feet and to wipe them with the towel with which he was girded.
Then he came to Simon Peter, and Peter said to him: Lord, are you going to wash my feet? The Savior answered and said to him: What I am doing you do not know now; you will know it afterward.
Then Peter said to him: You shall never wash my feet. The Savior answered him: If I do not wash you, you have no part with me.
Then Simon Peter said to him: Lord, not only my feet, but also my hands and my head.
Then the Savior said to him: Whoever is clean has no need except to wash his feet, but is entirely clean.
And you are clean, but not all of you. He knew who it was who would betray him; that is why he said: You are not all clean.
After he had washed their feet and taken up his garments, when he had reclined at table again, he said to them:
Do you know what I have done to you? You call me Master and Lord, and you say rightly, for so I am. If I, the Lord and Master, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet.
I have given you an example, so that as I have done to you, you should also do.
Truly, truly I say to you, a servant is not greater than his lord, nor is the apostle greater than the one who sent him. If you know these things, then you are blessed if you do them.
I do not speak of all of you: I know whom I have chosen, but this is so that the scripture may be fulfilled: he who eats bread with me has lifted up his heel against me.
From now on I tell you before it happens, so that when it is done you may believe that I am.
Truly, truly I say to you, he who receives anyone I send receives me; he who receives me receives the one who sent me.
On the first day of the Passover the disciples came to Jesus, saying: Where do you want us to prepare the Passover for you to eat?
Then Jesus said: Go into the city, and as you go in, a man carrying a jar of water will come to meet you. Follow him into the house that he enters, to a certain man.
And then say to the master of the house: The Master says: My time is near; I am keeping the Passover with you, with my disciples.
And he will show you a large upper room, furnished, and prepare it for us there.
Then his disciples went and found it as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
When evening had come, he came and sat down with his twelve disciples, and as they were eating he said:
With desire I have desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer. I tell you that from now on I will not eat it with you until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.
When he had said these things, he was troubled in his spirit, and he declared openly and said: Truly, truly I say to you that one of you will betray me.
Then they began to be sorrowful and to say one by one: Is it I, Lord?
He said to them: He who dips his hand with me in this dish will betray me.
The Son of Man goes, as it is written of him. Woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would have been good for that man if he had not been born.
Then the disciples looked at one another, unsure of whom he was speaking, and asked among themselves which of them it was that would do such a thing.
One of his disciples, whom Jesus loved, was then reclining in Jesus's lap. Simon Peter beckoned to him and said to him: Who is it that he is speaking of?
So, leaning on Jesus's breast, he said to him: Lord, who is it? Jesus answered him: It is the one to whom I give the dipped bread.
When he had dipped the bread, he gave it to Judas Iscariot, son of Simon.
And after the morsel, Satan entered into him. Then Jesus said to him: What you are doing, do quickly.

None of those sitting at table knew why he said this to him. Because Judas had the purse, some thought that Jesus was telling him: Buy what we need for the feast day, or that he should give something to the poor.
Then Judas, who betrayed him, answered and said: Is it I, Master? Then he said to him: You have said it.
When he had received the morsel, he went out at once; and at once it was night. When he had gone out, Jesus said:
Now the Son of Man is glorified, and God is glorified in him; and God will glorify him in himself, and at once glorified him.
While they were sitting at table, the Savior took bread, blessed it, broke it and gave it to his disciples, saying: "Take and eat. This is my body, which is given for you."

Then he took the cup, gave thanks, blessed it and gave it to them, saying: "Drink from this, all of you. This is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for you and for many for the forgiveness of sins."
"I tell you: from now on I will not drink of this fruit of the vine until the day when I drink it new with you in my Father's kingdom. Do this in remembrance of me."

Then the Lord said: "Simon, Simon, see, Satan has asked for you all, so that he may sift you like wheat. I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail; and when you have once turned back, strengthen your brothers."
"Little children, I am with you only a little while longer. You will look for me, and as I said to the Jews, 'Where I am going, you cannot come,' so I say to you now."
"A new commandment I give you now: that you love one another. As I have loved you, so you should love one another."
"By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another."
Then Simon Peter said to him: "Lord, where are you going?" The Savior answered him: "Where I am going, you cannot follow me now; you will follow me afterward."

Then the Savior said to them: "All of you will stumble because of me this night. It is written: I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered. But after I have risen, I will go ahead of you into Galilee."
Then Peter answered and said to him: "Even if all of them stumble because of you, I will never stumble, I who am ready to go with you either to prison or to death. I will lay down my life for you."
Then the Savior answered: "You will lay down your life for me? Truly, truly I tell you, this very night, before the cock crows, you will deny me three times."
Then Peter said to him: "[?] Even if I must die with you, I will not deny you." All the disciples said the same.

"Do not let your hearts be troubled. You believe in God; believe also in me. In my Father's house there are many dwelling places. If it were not so, I would have told you, for I am going to prepare a place for you. And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and take you to myself, so that where I am, you may be also. And you know where I am going, and you know the way."
Then Thomas said to him: "Lord, we do not know where you are going; how can we know the way?"

Then the Savior said to him: "I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me. If you had known me, you would have known my Father too. From now on you know him, and you have seen him."
Then Philip said to him: "Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us."
Then the Savior said to him: "I have been with you all for so long, and you have not known me?"
"Philip, whoever sees me sees the Father. How can you say, 'Show us the Father'? Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in me?"

The words that I speak to you I do not speak from myself: the Father, dwelling in me, he does the works. Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in me? Otherwise, believe because of the works themselves.

Truly, truly I say to you: whoever believes in me, the works that I do he also does, because I go to the Father; and whatever you ask in my name, that I will do, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
If you love me, then you will keep my commandments, and I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Comforter, so that he may dwell with you forever,
the Spirit of truth, whom this world cannot receive, because it does not see him and does not know him. You know him, because he dwells with you and is in you.
I will not leave you orphans: I am coming to you. Yet a little while, and this world will no longer see me; but you will see me, because I live and you live.
On that day you will understand that I am in my Father, and you in me, and I in you.
Whoever has my commandments and keeps them, he is the one who loves me; and whoever loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and will show myself to him.
Then Judas, not the one called Iscariot, said to him: Lord, what has happened, that you will reveal yourself to us and not to this world?
Then the Saviour answered and said to him: If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our dwelling with him.
Whoever does not love me does not keep my words; and the word that you have heard is not mine, but the Father's who sent me.

These things I have spoken to you while I dwell with you. The Comforter, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things and will bring to your mind everything that I have said to you.
I leave you peace; my peace I give to you. I do not give to you as this world gives.
Let your heart not be troubled, and do not be afraid. You have heard what I said to you: I go away, and I am coming to you.

If you loved me, then you would rejoice that I am going to the Father, because the Father is greater than I. And now I tell you before it happens, so that when it has happened you may believe it. I will no longer speak much with you, for the prince of this world is coming, and he has nothing in me. But so that this world may understand that I love the Father, I do as the Father commanded me.
And he said to them: When I sent you out without purse and bag and shoes, did you lack anything? They said to him: Nothing.
Then he said to them: But now whoever has a purse, let him take it, and likewise his bag; and whoever has none, let him sell his tunic and buy a sword.
For I tell you that what is written must still be fulfilled in me: 'And he was counted among the wicked.' For the things concerning me are coming to an end.
Then they said: Lord, look, here are two swords. Then he said to them: It is enough. Get up, and let us go from here.
And when they had sung the hymn, they went out, as was their custom, to the Mount of Olives.

Then he said to them: I am the true vine, and my Father is the vinedresser. Every branch in me that does not bear fruit, he takes away; and every one that bears fruit, he cleanses, so that it may bear more fruit.
You are already clean because of the word that I have spoken to you. Abide in me, and I in you.
Just as the branch cannot bear fruit by itself unless it abides in the vine, so neither can you unless you abide in me.
I am the vine, and you are the branches. Whoever abides in me, and I in him, bears much fruit, for without me you can do nothing.
If anyone does not abide in me, he is thrown out like a branch and withers; and they gather them and throw them into the fire, and they burn.
If you abide in me and my words abide in you, ask whatever you wish, and it will be done for you.
My Father is glorified in this: that you bring forth much fruit and become my disciples.
As my Father has loved me, so I have loved you. Abide in my love.
If you keep my commandments, then you will abide in my love, just as I have kept my Father's commandment and abide in his love.
I have said this to you so that my joy may be fulfilled. This is my commandment: that you love one another as I have loved you.
No one has greater love than this: that someone lays down his life for his friends. You are my friends if you do what I command you.
I no longer call you servants, for the servant does not know what his lord is doing. I call you friends, because I have made known to you everything that I have heard from my Father.
You did not choose me, but I chose you, and I appointed you to go and bring forth fruit, and that your fruit should abide, so that whatever you ask the Father in my name, he may give it to you.
This I command you: that you love one another.
If this world hates you, know then that it hated me before you.
