If you were of this world, this world would love what was its own. But because you are not of the world, but I chose you out of the world, therefore the world hates you.
Remember the word that I said to you: a servant is not greater than his lord.
If they persecuted me, then they will persecute you too; if they kept my word, then they will keep yours.
But they will do all these things to you because of my name, for they do not know him who sent me.
If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin.
Whoever hates me hates my Father. If I had not done among them [?] works that no one else does, they would not have sin.
But now they have seen and have hated both me and my Father. But this is so that the word written in their law may be fulfilled: for they hated me without cause.
When the Comforter comes, whom I will send you from the Father, the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father, he will bear witness about me.
And you also will bear witness, because you have been with me from the beginning.

I tell you these things so that you will not be made to stumble. They will put you out of their synagogues; and the time is coming when everyone who kills you will think he is offering service to God. They will do these things because they have not known my Father, nor me.
But I tell you these things so that when their time comes, you will remember that I told you about it beforehand.
I did not tell you these things from the beginning, because I was with you. Now I am going to the one who sent me, and none of you asks me, "Where are you going?"
But because I have told you these things, sorrow has filled your heart.
But I tell you the truth: it is good for you that I go. If I do not go, the Comforter will not come to you; if I go, I will send him to you.
And when he comes, he will convict the world of sin, of righteousness, and of judgment.
Of sin, because they do not believe in me; of righteousness, because I am going to the Father and you will no longer see me; of judgment, because the prince of this world has been judged.
I still have many things to tell you, but you cannot bear them now. When the Spirit of truth comes, he will teach you all truth.
He will not speak on his own, but he will speak whatever he hears, and he will tell you the things that are to come.
He will glorify me, because he has received from what is mine and will tell it to you.
Everything the Father has is mine. That is why I said that he receives from what is mine and will tell it to you.
In a little while you will not see me, and again in a little while you will see me, because I am going to my Father.

Then some of his disciples said to one another, "What is this he is telling us: 'In a little while you will not see me, and again in a little while you will see me,' and 'I am going to the Father'?" Then they said, "What does he mean by 'a little while'? We do not know what he is saying."

Then the Savior knew that they wanted to ask him, and he said to them, "Are you asking one another about this, that I said, 'In a little while you will not see me, and again in a little while you will see me'?
Truly, truly I tell you, you will weep and lament, but this world will rejoice. You will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will be turned into joy.

When a woman gives birth she has sorrow, because her hour has come. But when she has borne the child, she no longer remembers the pain, because of her joy that a human being has been born into the world.
So you also have sorrow now. But I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you. On that day you will not ask me anything.
Truly, truly I tell you, if you ask the Father for anything in my name, he will give it to you.
Until now you have asked for nothing in my name. Ask, and you will receive, so that your joy may be full.
I have told you these things in parables. The time is coming when I will no longer speak to you in parables, but will tell you plainly about the Father.
On that day you will ask in my name, and I do not tell you that I will ask the Father on your behalf.
For the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me and have believed that I came out from God.
I came out from the Father and came into the world; now I am leaving the world again and going to the Father.
Then his disciples said to him: Behold, now you speak openly and say no figure of speech.
Now we know that you know all things, and you have no need for anyone to ask you; by this we believe that you came forth from God.

Then the Savior answered them: Do you believe now? Behold, the hour is coming, and has now come, when you will be scattered, each one to his own, and will leave me alone; and yet I am not alone, for the Father is with me.
These things I have spoken to you, so that in me you may have peace.
In this world you have tribulation, but take courage: I have overcome this world.

The Savior spoke these things, and with his eyes lifted up to heaven he said to the Father: The hour has come; glorify your Son, so that your Son may glorify you, just as you gave him power over all flesh, so that he may give eternal life to all whom you have given him.
This is eternal life: that they know you, the one true God, and him whom you sent, the Savior Christ.
I have glorified you on earth; I have finished the work that you gave me to do. And now glorify me, Father, with yourself, in the glory that I had with you before the world existed.
I have made your name known to the people whom you gave me out of the world. They were yours, and you gave them to me, and they have kept your word.

Now they have understood that everything you gave me comes from you, for the words that you gave me I have given to them, and they received them and understood truly that I came forth from you, and they believed that you sent me.
And I pray for them: I do not pray for the world, but for those whom you gave me, for they are yours, and all that is mine is yours, and all that is yours is mine.
And I am glorified in them. And I am no longer in the world, but these are in the world, and I am coming to you, holy Father.
Keep in your name those whom you gave me, so that they may be one, just as we are.
While I was with them, I kept them in your name. Those whom you gave me I have kept, and none of them is lost except the son of perdition, so that the scripture might be fulfilled.
Now I am coming to you, and I speak these things in the world so that they may have my joy fulfilled in themselves.
I have given them your word, and the world has hated them, because they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.
I do not ask that you take them out of the world, but that you keep them from evil. They are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.
Sanctify them in truth: your word is truth.
As you sent me into the world, so I have sent them into the world, and for their sake I sanctify myself, so that they themselves may also be sanctified in truth.

I do not pray for these alone, but also for those who will believe in me through their word, that they may all be one, as you, Father, are in me and I in you, that they too may be one in us, so that the world may believe that you sent me.

And the glory that you gave me I have given to them, so that they may be one, just as we are one: I in them and you in me, so that they may be made perfect in one, and the world may know that you sent me and loved them, as you loved me.
Father, those whom you gave me, I will that where I am they may be with me, so that they may see my glory which you gave me, for you loved me before the making of the world.

Righteous Father, the world did not know you, but I knew you, and these knew that you sent me. And I made your name known to them and will make it known, so that the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I also in them.
Then the Saviour came into the village that is called Gethsemane, across the brook Kidron. There was a garden there, and he and his disciples went into it.
Judas, who betrayed him, knew the place, because the Saviour often came there with his disciples.
When he came to the place, he said to his disciples: Sit here and pray, so that you do not enter into temptation, while I go over there and pray.
And taking Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, James and John, he began to be sorrowful and to mourn.
Then he said to them: My soul is sorrowful even unto death. Wait here and watch with me.
And then he went away from them about a stone's throw, and kneeling down he fell on his face and prayed that, if it were possible, the hour might pass from him, saying:
Father, if it is possible — Father, Father, all things are possible for you — my Father, if it is possible, take this cup away from me! Yet not what I will, but what you will.
And when he rose from his prayer, he came to his disciples and found them sleeping
and said to them: Why are you sleeping? Could you not watch with me for one hour?
Watch and pray, so that you do not enter into temptation.
The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.
Again he went a second time and prayed. Then an angel from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him. He was then brought into great earnestness [anguish]
and prayed longer, saying: My Father, if this cup cannot pass by unless I drink it, your will be done.
Then his sweat became like drops of blood running down to the earth.
And when he rose, he came again to his disciples and found them sleeping because of their sorrow.
Their eyes were heavy, and they did not know what to answer him.
And leaving them, he went again and prayed a third time, saying the same words.
Then he came to his disciples and said to them: Sleep and rest. Now the hour draws near, and the Son of Man will be betrayed into the hands of sinners.
Rise, let us go. Behold, now the one who betrays me draws near.

And while he was still speaking, behold, Judas, one of the twelve, having received the band of soldiers, came, and with him a great crowd with lanterns and torches and weapons, with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and from the scribes and from the elders of the people.
The one who betrayed him had given them this sign, saying: Whomever I kiss, that is the one. Seize him and lead him away.
And going quickly up to the Saviour he said: Hail, master! And he drew near to the Saviour to kiss him.
The Saviour said to him: Judas, do you betray the Son of Man with a kiss? Friend, why have you come? And he kissed him.
Then Jesus, truly knowing all the things that were to come upon him, went forth and said to them: "Whom do you seek?" They answered him: "Jesus of Nazareth." Then Jesus said to them: "I am he."
And Judas, who betrayed him, stood with them.
When he said to them, "I am he," they went backward and then fell to the ground.
Again he asked them: "Whom do you seek?" They said: "Jesus of Nazareth." Then Jesus answered: "I told you that I am he.
If you seek me, let these men go away." This was so that the word he had spoken might be fulfilled: "Of those whom you gave me, I have not lost any."
Then they came up and laid their hands on Jesus and held him.
When those who were around him saw what was about to happen, they said to him: "Lord, shall we strike with the sword?"
Simon Peter, who had a sword, drew it out and struck the high priest's servant and cut off his right ear; the servant's name was Malchus.
Then Jesus said to Peter: "The cup that the Father has given me, shall I not drink it? Put your sword into its sheath.
All who take the sword shall perish by the sword.
Or do you think that I cannot ask my Father, and he would now provide me with more than twelve thousand hosts of angels? How then would the scriptures be fulfilled, that it must happen this way?"
"Let it be, up to this point!" And when he touched the servant's ear, he healed it.
At that time Jesus said to the crowds: "You have come out with swords and clubs to seize me, as if against a thief.
Day after day I was with you, teaching in the temple, and you did not seize me. But this is your hour and the power of darkness."
This was done so that the scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled.
Then all his disciples abandoned him and fled. The cohort, its commander, and the officers of the Jews seized Jesus, bound him, and led him first to Annas.
He was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was high priest that year. It was Caiaphas who had advised the Jews that it was better for one man to die for the people.
A certain young man followed him, wearing a linen cloth over his naked body, and they seized him. But he threw off the linen cloth and fled from them naked.
Then Simon Peter and another disciple followed Jesus at a distance, as far as the courtyard of the high priest.
That disciple was known to the high priest, and he went in with Jesus into the high priest's courtyard. Peter stood outside at the door.
The other disciple, the one known to the high priest, went out, spoke to the woman keeping the door, and brought Peter in.
When the doorkeeper saw him and was looking at him, she said: "Are you one of this man's disciples?" He said to the woman: "I do not know him, nor do I know what you are saying."
The servants and the officers were standing at the fire, because it was cold, and were warming themselves. Peter was standing with them and warming himself, so that he might see how it would end.
The high priest asked Jesus about his disciples and about his teaching.
Then Jesus answered him: I have spoken openly to this world; I always taught in the synagogue and in the temple, where all the Jews come together, and I said nothing in secret.
Why do you ask me? Ask those who heard what I said to them: behold, they know what I said.
When he had said these things, one of the attendants standing by struck Jesus with his hand, saying: Is that how you answer the high priest?
Then Jesus answered him: If I have spoken wrongly, bear witness to the wrong; if I have spoken rightly, why do you strike me?
Then Annas sent him bound to Caiaphas the high priest.
Simon Peter was standing outside in the courtyard, warming himself. Then another maidservant saw him and said to those standing around: This man too was with Jesus the Nazarene.
Then those who were standing there came up and said to Peter: Truly you are one of them; your speech gives you away, showing that you are a Galilean.
Then he denied it again with an oath: I do not know the man.
And after a little while, about an hour later, one of the servants of the high priest, a kinsman of the man whose ear Peter had cut off, said: Truly this man was with him, for he is a Galilean.

Did I not see you in the garden with him? Then he began to curse and to deny and to swear, saying: I do not know him, I do not know what you are saying, I do not know the man you are speaking of. And immediately the cock crowed.

And the Lord turned and looked at Peter, and Peter remembered the word of the Lord that he had said to him: Before the cock crows, you will deny me three times today. And Peter went out and wept bitterly.
When morning had come, all the chief priests came with the elders of the people and with the scribes, holding council; they sought false testimony against Jesus so that they might put him to death,
and they found none; though many false witnesses came forward, still they found none, and their testimonies did not agree.
At last two false witnesses came and said: We heard him say that he could destroy the temple of God that is made with hands, and after three days build another not made with hands.
Jesus was silent. The chief of the priests rose up in their midst and questioned Jesus, saying: Do you answer nothing to what these men testify against you? Jesus answered nothing.
And again the high priest said to him: I adjure you by the living God to tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of the blessed God.
Then Jesus said to him: You have said it. And he said to them: If I tell you, you will not believe me; and if I ask you, you will neither answer me nor let me go.
Yet truly I say to you: from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the power of God and coming on the clouds of heaven.
Then the chief of the priests tore his garments, saying: He has blasphemed.
What further need do we have of witnesses? Behold, now you have heard blasphemy from his own mouth: what do you think?
Then they all answered and said: He is guilty and deserves death.
Then they spat in his face; those who were holding him mocked him, covered his face, and struck him with their fists.
Others struck him in the face with the flat of their hands, saying: "Prophesy to us, Christ: who is it that strikes you?" And they said many other things against him, blaspheming.

And they led him bound into the praetorium and handed him over to the governor Pontius Pilate. They themselves did not go into the praetorium, so that they would not be defiled but could eat the Passover.

Then Judas, who had betrayed him, saw that he had been condemned. Moved by remorse, he brought the thirty pennies back to the chief priests and the elders, saying: "I have sinned in betraying righteous blood."
Then they said: "What is that to us? You see to it."
And he threw the pieces of silver into the temple and went away, and he went and hanged himself with a rope.
The chief priests took the pieces of silver and said: "It is not lawful to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood."

After they had taken counsel, they used the money to buy the potter's field as a burial place for strangers. For this reason that field has been called Akeldama, the field of blood, to this present day.

Then what had been spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled, when he said: "They took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of the one who was valued, on whom the children of Israel set a price, and they gave them for the potter's field, as the Lord directed me."
Then Pilate went out to them and said: "What accusation do you bring against this man?"

Then they answered and said to him: "If this man were not an evildoer, we would not have handed him over to you. We found this man misleading our people, forbidding the payment of tribute to Caesar, and saying that he himself is Christ, a king."

Then Pilate said to them: "Take him yourselves and judge him according to your law." Then the Jews said: "It is not lawful for us to put anyone to death." This happened so that the word of the Lord would be fulfilled, which he spoke to signify by what death he was to die.
Then Pilate went back into the judgment hall, called Jesus, and said to him: "Are you the king of the Jews?"
Then Jesus answered: "Do you say this of your own accord, or did others tell you this about me?"
Then Pilate answered: "Am I a Jew? Your own people and the chief priests handed you over to me. What have you done?"

Then Jesus answered: "My kingdom is not of this world. If my kingdom were of this world, my servants would fight so that I would not be handed over to the Jews. But as it is, my kingdom is not from here."
Then Pilate said to him: "So are you a king?" Then Jesus answered: "You say that I am a king.
For this I was born, and for this I came into the world: to bear witness to the truth.
Everyone who is of the truth hears my voice." Then Pilate said to him: "What is truth?"
When he had said this, he went out again to the Jews and said to the chief priests and to the crowd: "I find no guilt at all in this man."
But they insisted all the more, saying: "He stirs up the people, teaching throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee all the way to here."
When Pilate heard "Galilee," he asked whether the man was a Galilean. And when he learned that he came under Herod's jurisdiction, he sent him on to Herod, who was himself in Jerusalem in those days.
When Herod saw Jesus he was very glad. He had wanted to see him for a long time, because he had heard many things about him and hoped to see some sign done by him.
He questioned him at length, but he gave him no answer at all.
The chief priests and the scribes stood there, accusing him relentlessly.
Herod and his soldiers treated him with contempt and mocked him. They dressed him in a white garment, and Herod sent him back to Pilate.
Herod and Pilate became friends on that day. Before that, they had been enemies.
Pilate called together the chief priests, the magistrates and the people. He went out to them and said to them: "You have brought me this man as one who leads the people astray.
Look, I am bringing him out to you, so that you may understand that I have found no case against him in any of the things you accuse him of.
Neither did Herod, for I sent you back to him, and look, he has done nothing that deserves death. I will have him punished and then release him."
Then the whole crowd cried out, saying: "Take this man away! Crucify him, crucify him!"
Then Pilate said to them: "Take him yourselves and crucify him. I find no case against him."
The Jews answered him: "We have a law, and by that law he must die, because he made himself the Son of God."
When Pilate heard this, he was even more afraid. He went back into the praetorium and said to Jesus: "Where are you from?" Jesus gave him no answer.
Then Pilate said to him: "Will you not speak to me? Do you not know that I have power to crucify you and power to release you?"
Jesus answered: "You would have no power over me at all if it had not been given to you from above. Therefore the one who handed me over to you has the greater sin."
From then on Pilate tried to release him. But the Jews cried out, saying: "If you release this man, you are no friend of Caesar. Anyone who makes himself king speaks against Caesar."
When Pilate heard these words, he led Jesus out and sat on his judgment seat at the place called Lithostrotos, in Hebrew Gabbatha.
It was the day of preparation before the Passover, about the sixth hour. He said to the Jews: "Here is your king!" Then they cried out: "Take him away, take him away, and crucify him!"
Pilate said to them: "Shall I crucify your king?" The priests answered: "We have no king but Caesar." The chief priests accused him of many things. Jesus gave no answer.
Then Pilate said to him: "Do you not hear how many testimonies they bring against you?" But he did not answer him a single word, so that the governor was greatly amazed.
At the feast it was the governor's custom to release to the people one of the prisoners, whoever they asked for.
At that time he had a notorious prisoner named Barabbas.
When they had gathered, Pilate said: "You have a custom that I release one prisoner to you at the Passover. Whom do you want me to release to you, Barabbas or Jesus, who is called Christ?"
He knew that they had handed him over out of envy.
While he was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent to him, saying: "Have nothing to do with that righteous man, for I have suffered many things today in a vision because of him."
The chief of the high priests and the elders persuaded the people to ask for Barabbas, so that they might destroy the Savior.
Then the governor answered and said to them: "Which of these two do you want me to release to you?" Then they said: "Barabbas."
This Barabbas was a robber, who had been bound in prison for a certain uprising that had taken place in the city, and for murder.
Then Pilate said to them: "What shall I do with the Savior, who is called Christ?" They all said: "Let him be crucified!"
Then the governor said to them: "What evil has he done?" Then they cried out all the more, saying: "Let him be crucified!"

Then Pilate saw that it did no good at all, but that the uproar was growing instead. He took water and washed his hands before the people, saying: "I am innocent of the blood of this righteous man. See to it yourselves."
Then all the people answered and said: "His blood be on us and on our children!"
Then he released Barabbas to them; and he had the Savior scourged and handed him over to them to be crucified.
The governor's soldiers took the Savior into the praetorium and gathered the whole cohort around him. They stripped him and dressed him in a purple tunic, and put a red cloak around him.
They wove a crown of thorns and set it on his head, and put a reed in his right hand. They bent the knee before him and mocked him, saying: "Hail, King of the Jews!"
They spat on him, took the reed, and struck him on the head.
After they had mocked him, they stripped him of the cloak and the purple, dressed him in his own clothes, and led him away to crucify him, carrying his cross.
As they [?] him, they found a man of Cyrene coming from the country, named Simon, the father of Alexander and Rufus. They forced him to carry the cross behind the Savior.
A great multitude of people followed him, and of women, who mourned and lamented him.
Then the Savior turned to them and said: "Children of Jerusalem, do not weep over me, but weep over yourselves and over your children.
For the days are coming now in which you will say: Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that did not bear, and the breasts that did not give suck.
Then they will begin to say to the mountains: Fall on us! and to the hills: Cover us!
For if they do these things to the green tree, what will happen to the dry?"
Two other evildoers were also led out with him to be put to death.
After that they came to the place called Golgotha, which is interpreted as the Place of the Skull.
They gave him wine mixed with myrrh and gall to drink, and when he had tasted it, he would not drink it.
The Savior said: "Father, forgive them for it, for they do not know what they are doing."
After they had crucified him, they took his clothes and divided them into four parts, one part for each soldier, and they also took the tunic.
The tunic was without seam, woven in one piece from the top all the way through.
Then they said among themselves: "Let us not tear it, but let us cast lots for it, to see whose it shall be."
So that the scripture might be fulfilled, which says: "They divided my garments among them, and for my garment they cast lots." And the soldiers did these things.
And they sat and kept watch over him.
And Pilate wrote a title stating his charge and set it over his head: "This is Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews."
Many of the Jews read this title, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city, and it was written in Hebrew, in Greek and in Latin.
Then the chief priests of the Jews said to Pilate: "Do not write 'King of the Jews.'"
Then Pilate answered: "What I have written, I have written."
Then two thieves were crucified with him, one on the right and the other on his left.
Those who passed by mocked him, shaking their heads and saying: "Ah, you who destroy the temple and build it again in three days, save yourself! If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross."

Likewise the chief priests, mocking him along with the scribes and the elders, said: "He made others whole; himself he cannot save. If he is the King of Israel, let him come down from the cross, and we will see it and believe him. He trusted in God; so let God deliver him now, if he wants him. For he said: 'I am the Son of God.'"
In the same way one of the thieves who were hanging there mocked him, saying: "If you are the Christ, save yourself and us."

Then the other answered and rebuked him, saying: "Do you not even fear God, seeing that you are under the same condemnation? And we indeed justly, for we are receiving what our deeds deserve; but this man has truly done nothing wrong."
And he said to Jesus: "Lord, remember me when you come into your kingdom."
Then Jesus said to him: "Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in paradise."
Standing by the cross of Jesus were his mother and his mother's sister, Mary the wife of Cleophas, and Mary Magdalene.
When Jesus saw his mother and the disciple whom he loved standing there, he said to his mother: "Woman, behold your son!"
After that he said to the disciple: "Behold your mother!" And from that hour the disciple took her into his own home.
From the sixth hour there was darkness over all the earth until the ninth hour.
And about the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, saying: "Heli, heli, lama sabacthani?" which is interpreted: "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?"
But some of those standing there who heard it said: "This man is calling Elijah."
After that, Jesus, knowing that all things were now finished, said, so that the scripture might be fulfilled: "I thirst."
A vessel full of vinegar had been set there,
And immediately one of them ran, took a sponge, filled it with vinegar, put it on a reed and gave it to him to drink.
When Jesus had received the vinegar, he said: "It is finished."
The others said: "Leave him now; let us see whether Elijah comes to deliver him."
But the Savior cried out with a loud voice: Father, into your hands I commend my spirit! And with his head bowed he gave up the spirit.
Behold, then the veil of the temple was torn in two, from the top down to the bottom.
And the earth was shaken, and rocks were split, and tombs were opened.
And many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep there arose.
And going out from the tombs after his resurrection, they came into the holy city and appeared to many.
The centurion and those who were with him guarding the Savior, when they saw the earthquake and the things that happened there, were greatly afraid,
glorifying God and saying: This man is truly righteous, truly the Son of God.
And all the crowd of those who were gathered together for this spectacle and saw the things that happened there turned back, beating their breasts. Far off [?]
And many women, who had come up together with him from Galilee to Jerusalem,

among whom was Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the Less and of Joseph, and Salome the mother of the sons of Zebedee, who had followed him when he was in Galilee, were watching these things.

Then the Jews, because it was Friday, so that the bodies should not remain on the cross on the Sabbath (for that Sabbath was indeed a great one), asked Pilate that they might break their legs and have them taken away.
The soldiers came and broke the legs of the first, and of the other who was crucified with him.
When they came to the Savior and saw that he was already dead, they did not break his legs.

But one of the soldiers opened his side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out. This was so that the scripture would be fulfilled: You shall not break a bone of him. And another scripture says: They shall look on him whom they pierced.
When it had become evening, there came a certain rich man, a noble official, from Arimathea, a city of the Jews, named Joseph,
a good and righteous man, who was a disciple of the Savior, but secretly, for fear of the Jews; he was waiting for the kingdom of God.
He had not consented to their injustice and their deed.
He went to Pilate and asked for the Savior's body.
Pilate wondered whether he had already died, and he summoned the centurion and asked him whether he had already died. And when he learned it, he ordered that the body be given.
And then Nicodemus also came, who had first come to the Savior by night, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred pounds of it.
Then they received the Savior's body and bound it in linen cloths with the spices, as is the custom of the Jews in burying.
There was a garden in the place where he was crucified, and in the garden a new tomb, in which no one had yet been laid.
And Joseph laid it there, and rolled a great stone against the door of the tomb, and went away.
Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting opposite the tomb; they saw how his body was laid,
and turning back, they prepared spices and ointment, so that they might come and anoint him.
And on the sabbath they kept quiet, as the commandment required.
On the next day, which is Friday, the chief priests and the Pharisees came to Pilate,
saying: "Lord, we remember that that deceiver said while he was still alive: 'After three days I will rise.'

Order the tomb to be guarded until the third day, so that his disciples do not come and steal him and say to the people, 'He has risen from the dead.' Then the last error will be worse than the first."
Then Pilate said to them: "You have guards. Go and guard it as you know how." So they went from there and made the tomb secure, sealing the stone, with the guards.
In the evening of the sabbath, as it dawned toward the first day of the week, while it was still dark,
Mary Magdalene and the other Mary and Salome came to the tomb. They carried the spices they had prepared.
And as the sun was rising they said among themselves: "Who will roll the stone away for us from the door of the tomb?" It was very large.
And behold, there had been a great earthquake. An angel of God came down from heaven, went up to the tomb and rolled the stone away.
And when they looked, they saw that the stone had been rolled away from the tomb and an angel was sitting on it.
His appearance was like lightning and his clothing was like snow.
The guards were terrified out of fear of him and became like dead men.
Then the angel answered and said to the women: "Do not be afraid. I know that you are looking for Jesus, who was crucified.
He is not here. He has risen, as he said. Come and see the place where the Lord was laid."
And then it happened, while they were frightened in their minds by this,
behold, two men in shining clothing stood near them.
As they were afraid and bowed their faces to the ground, the men said to them: "Why do you look for the living among the dead? He is not here, but he has risen.
Remember how he spoke to you while he was still in Galilee, saying that the Son of Man must be handed over into the hands of sinful men, be crucified, and rise again on the third day.
And go quickly and tell his disciples that he has risen from the dead. And behold, he is going ahead of you into Galilee; there you will see him. Behold, he told you this beforehand."
And then they remembered his words, and they left the tomb quickly with fear and with great joy, running to tell his disciples.
She ran and came to Simon Peter and to the other disciple, the one Jesus loved, and said to them: "They have taken my Lord from the tomb, and I do not know where they have put him."
Then Peter and the other disciple went out and came to the tomb.
The two ran together, and the other disciple ran faster than Peter and reached the tomb first.
And when he bent down, he saw the linen cloths lying there, but he did not go in.

Then Simon Peter came following him, and went into the tomb and saw the linen cloths lying there, and the face-cloth that had been over his head, not lying with the linen cloths but wrapped up separately in a place by itself.

Then the disciple who had come to the tomb first also went in, and he saw and believed. For as yet they did not know the Scripture, that he had to rise from the dead. Then the disciples went back again to their own homes.
Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven devils, stood outside at the tomb weeping.
While she was weeping, [someone] said to her: "Woman, why are you weeping?" She said to him: "Because they have taken away my Lord, and I do not know where they have laid him."
When she had said this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing there, and did not know that it was Jesus. Then Jesus said to her: "Woman, why are you weeping? Whom are you looking for?"
She, thinking that it was the gardener, said to him: "Lord, if you have taken him away, tell me where you have laid him, so that I may take him."
Then Jesus said to her: "Mary!" She turned and said to him: "Rabboni!", which means "Master."
Then Jesus said to her: "Do not touch me, for I have not yet ascended to my Father.
Go to my brothers and say to them: I am ascending to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God."
Then, behold, some of the guards came into the city and told the chief priests everything that had been done there.

And when they had gathered with the elders and taken counsel, they gave a sufficient sum of money to the soldiers, saying: "Say this: 'His disciples came by night and stole him away while we were sleeping.'
And if the governor hears of this, we will persuade him and keep you free from worry."
So they took the money and did as they had been instructed, and this story has been spread abroad among the Jews to this day.
Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples: "I have seen the Lord, and he said these things to me."
And then, behold, Jesus came to meet them, saying: "Greetings!" They came up to him, took hold of his feet, and worshipped him.
Then Jesus said to them: "Do not be afraid. Go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee; there they will see me."
As they went away from there, they told all these things to the eleven, who were mourning and weeping, and to all the others who had been with him.
And when they heard that he was alive and had been seen by them, they did not believe them. These words seemed to them like madness, and they did not believe them.
After this he appeared to two of them as they were walking, going that same day to a village a hundred and sixty stadia away from Jerusalem, named Emmaus.
And they were talking with each other about all the things that had happened. And it came to pass, while they were talking and discussing together,
that Jesus himself drew near and went along with them. Their eyes were held, so that they did not recognize him.
And he said to them: "What are these things that you are discussing with each other as you walk, and why are you sad?"

And then one of them, whose name was Cleopas, answered and said to him: "Are you the only stranger in Jerusalem, and do you not know the things that have been done there in these days?" Then he said: "What things?"

And they said: "About Jesus the Nazarene, who was a man, a prophet mighty in deed and in word before God and before all the people; and how the chief priests and our rulers handed him over to be condemned to death, and crucified him.
We hoped that he was the one who would redeem Israel. And now, besides all this, today is the third day since these things were done.
Also some women of our company frightened us; they were at the tomb before daylight,
and when they did not find his body, they came saying that they had certainly seen a vision of angels, who say that he is alive.
And some of us went to the tomb and found it just as the women had said; but him they certainly did not find."
And he said to them: "O foolish ones, slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken!
Was it not necessary for Christ to suffer these things and to enter into his glory?"
And beginning from Moses and from all the prophets, he explained to them in all the scriptures the things that concerned him.
And then they drew near to the village to which they were going, and he made as if he would go farther.
And they urged him, saying: "Stay with us, for it is evening and the day is already far spent." And he went in with them.
And it happened then, while he sat at table with them, that he took the bread and blessed it and broke it and gave it to them.
And their eyes were opened, and they recognized him; and he vanished from their sight.
And they said to one another: "Was not our heart burning within us while he spoke on the way and opened the scriptures to us?"
And rising at that same hour, they returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven gathered together, and those who were with them, saying that the Lord had truly risen and had appeared to Simon.
And they told what had happened on the way, and how they had recognized him in the breaking of the bread. But they did not believe them either.
While they were saying these things, when it was late on that same day, the first day of the week, and the doors were shut where the disciples were, for fear of the Jews,
Jesus came and stood in the midst of his disciples and said to them: "Peace be with you. It is I; do not be afraid."
Troubled and terrified, they thought they were seeing a spirit.
Then he said to them: "Why are you troubled, and why do thoughts arise in your hearts?
See my hands and feet, that it is I myself. Touch me and see, because a spirit does not have flesh and bones, as you see that I have."
And when he had said this, he showed them his hands, his feet and his side.
And while they still did not believe and were marvelling for joy, he said: "Have you anything here that can be eaten?"
Then they brought him a piece of roasted fish and a honeycomb. And when he had eaten in front of them, he took what was left and gave it to them.
And he said to them: These are the words that I spoke to you while I was still with you: that everything written about me in the law of Moses, in the prophets and in the psalms had to be fulfilled.
Then he opened their minds so that they could understand the Scriptures.

And he said to them: For thus it is written, and thus it was necessary for Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead on the third day, and for repentance and forgiveness of sins to be preached in his name to all nations, beginning from Jerusalem.
You are witnesses of these things, and I am sending the promise of my Father upon you.
Truly the disciples rejoiced when they saw the Lord.
Then he said to them again: Peace be with you. As the Father sent me, so I send you.
When he had said this, he breathed on them and said to them: Receive the Holy Spirit. Whoever's sins you forgive, they are forgiven them, and whoever's sins you retain, they are retained.
Thomas, one of the Twelve, who is called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came.
Then the other disciples said to him: We have seen the Lord.
Then he said to them: Unless I see in his hands the mark of the nails, and put my finger into the place of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe.
And after eight days his disciples were inside again, and Thomas with them.
Jesus came, though the doors were shut, and stood in their midst and said: Peace be with you!
Then he said to Thomas: Bring your finger here and see my hands, and bring your hand and put it into my side, and do not be unbelieving, but believing.
Then Thomas answered and said to him: My Lord and my God!
Then Jesus said to him: Because you have seen me, you have believed. Blessed are those who have not seen and have believed.
Jesus did many other signs in the sight of his disciples, which are not written in this book.
These are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in his name.
After this Jesus showed himself again at the sea called Tiberias. He showed himself in this way.
Together were Simon Peter, and Thomas who is called Didymus, and Nathanael, who was from Cana in Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two others of his disciples.
Then Simon Peter said to them: I am going fishing. Then they said to him: We will come with you. And they went out and got into a boat, and that night they caught nothing.
When morning had come, Jesus stood on the shore, yet the disciples did not know that it was Jesus.
Then Jesus said to them: Lads, do you have any food? They answered him: No.
Then he said to them: Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some.
So they cast it, and now they could not draw it in because of the great number of fish.
Then the disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter: It is the Lord.
When Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he girded himself with his tunic (for he was in fact naked) and threw himself into the sea.
The other disciples came in the boat. They were not far from land, only about two hundred cubits, dragging the net of fish.
When they then came up onto land, they saw coals lying there, and fish lying on them, and bread.
Then the Savior said to them: "Bring some of the fish that you have just caught."
Simon Peter then went up and drew the net to land, full of large fish, a hundred and fifty-three. And although they were so large, the net was not torn.
Then the Savior said to them: "Come and eat." And none of those sitting there dared to ask him, "Who are you?" They knew that it was the Lord.
And the Savior came and took bread and gave it to them, and likewise the fish.
This was now the third time that the Savior had appeared to the disciples since he rose from death.
When they had eaten, the Savior said to Simon Peter: "Simon, son of John, do you love me more than these?" He said to him: "Yes, Lord, you know that I love you." He said to him: "Feed my lambs."
Then he said to him again: "Simon, son of John, do you love me?" He said to him: "Yes, Lord, you know that I love you." Then he said to him: "Feed my lambs."

Then he said to him a third time: "Simon, son of John, do you love me?" Peter was then grieved because he had said to him a third time, "Do you love me?", and he said to him: "Lord, you know all things; you know that I love you." Then he said to him: "Feed my sheep.

Truly, truly I say to you: when you were younger, you girded yourself and went where you wished; when you grow old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will gird you and lead you where you do not wish to go."
He said this to signify by what death he was to glorify God.
When he had said this, he said to him: "Follow me."
Peter turned and saw following them the disciple whom the Savior loved, the one who had leaned on his breast at the supper and said: "Lord, who is it that betrays you?"
When Peter saw him, he said to the Savior: "Lord, what about this one?" The Savior said to him: "If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you? You follow me."
So the word went out among the brothers that this disciple would not die. Yet the Savior did not say to him that he would not die, but: "If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you?"
This is the disciple who bears witness about these things and who wrote these things, and we know that his testimony is true.
There are also many other things that the Savior did; if they were all written down, each one separately,
I do not think that even this world itself could contain the books that would have to be written.
The eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain that the Savior had appointed for them, and when they saw him they worshipped him, though some doubted.
And he reproached them for their unbelief and the hardness of their hearts, because they had not believed those who had seen him risen.
And he spoke to them, saying: "All power has been given to me in heaven and on earth."

Go into all the world, preach the gospel to every creature, and teach all peoples, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit; teach them to keep all things whatsoever I have commanded you.
And behold, I am with you all days until the end of the world.
Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved; but whoever does not believe will be condemned.
These signs will follow those who believe:
In my name they will cast out devils, they will speak with new tongues, they will take up serpents,
And if they drink anything deadly, it will not harm them.
They will lay hands on the sick, and they will be well.
Stay in the city until you are clothed with power from on high.

Then he led them out to Bethany, and lifting up his hands he blessed them. And it came to pass, while he was blessing them, that he departed from them and was carried up into heaven and sat at the right hand of God. And they, worshipping, returned to Jerusalem with great joy.
And they were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God,
And going forth they preached everywhere, the Lord working with them and confirming the word through the signs that followed.
